If the [MON] is the target of a healing spell, if it consumes a healing potion, or if it is affected by a similar magical effect, it gains a +2 bonus to its AC, it has advantage on Dexterity saving throws, and it can make one melee attack as a bonus action [DURATION].

The [MON] has [#] limbs. While it has more than [#] limbs, the [MON] is immune to being knocked prone or restrained. Whenever the [MON] takes [#] or more damage in a single turn, one of its limbs is destroyed. Each time a limb is destroyed after the [#]th one, the [MON] must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or be knocked prone.

When a creature hits the [MON] with a slashing or piercing melee weapon, the creature must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw, or its weapon becomes stuck to the [MON]'s shell. While the weapon is stuck, it can't be used. A creature can pull the weapon free by taking an action to make a DC [SAVE_DC] Strength check and succeeding.

If the [MON]'s razor line attack is available, a [MON] can use its movement to leap [#] ft in any direction by launching the wire like a spider's web so that it spears or snags an object, then immediately reeling it back in. It can carry up to 25 lb. of additional weight while moving this way. Moving this way doesn't expend its razor line attack.

The [MON] has three heads. While it has more than one head, the [MON] has advantage on saving throws against being blinded, charmed, deafened, frightened, and stunned. If the [MON] takes [#] or more damage in a single turn (and the damage isn't poison or psychic), one of its heads is severed. If all three of its heads are severed, the [MON] dies.

When a creature hits the [MON] with a weapon, it must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or the weapon sticks to the [MON]. A stuck weapon can't be used. A creature can take its action to remove one object from the [MON] by succeeding on a DC [SAVE_DC] Strength check. As a bonus action, the [MON] can release one weapon stuck to it.

When the [MON] dies, its mandibles remain locked in place continuing to grapple beyond its death. Until grapple ends creature takes [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage at the start of each of its turns as if the [MON] was still alive. Any creature can use an action to remove mandibles with successful DC [SAVE_DC] Strength (Athletics) or Wisdom (Medicine) check.

Each creature in the same water as the [MON] and that starts its turn within [#] ft of the [MON] must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or be poisoned while within this aura and [DURATION] after it leaves. A poisoned creature that starts its turn outside the aura can repeat this saving throw, ending the effect on itself on a success.

The [MON] generates a [#] ft radius aura of searing light and heat. A creature that starts its turn in the aura, or who enters it for the first time on a turn, takes [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage. The area in the aura is brightly lit, and it sheds dim light for another [#] ft. The aura dispels magical darkness of 3rd level or lower where the areas overlap.

The [MON]'s webs are anchored in the Material Plane and the Shadow Realm, existing in both simultaneously. Except for effects and attacks from the [MON], a creature in contact with or restrained by a [MON]'s webs has half cover and is immune to any spell or effect that would move it to a different plane, such as the banishment and plane shift spells.

A creature that enters a space within [#] ft of the [MON] or that starts its turn there must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or be affected as if by the calm emotions spell while it remains within [#] ft of the [MON]. This effect ends if the creature is attacked or harmed by a spell or if it witnesses any of its allies being harmed.

The [MON] is destroyed when reduced to 0 hit points, but it returns to unlife where it fell on the next nightfall with full hit points. It can be killed only by removing its head, burning the corpse, and dumping the ashes in the sea, or by returning it to its burial mound, placing an open pair of scissors on its chest, and driving pins through its ft.

If the [MON] fails a saving throw, it may choose to succeed instead and reflect the effect of the failed saving throw onto one hostile creature within [#] ft of it. The [MON] still suffers the effect of a successful saving throw, if any. The new target is entitled to a saving throw as if it were the original target of the attack, but with disadvantage.

When the [MON] is reduced to 0 hit points, it explodes into shards of hot stone and fire. Each creature within [#] ft of it must make a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw, taking [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a success. A [MON] is not immune to the fire damage of another [MON]'s death burst and doesn't absorb it.

The [MON]'s power waxes and wanes with the moon. Under a full moon, it has resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks and its weapon attacks deal an additional [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage. Under a new moon, it has vulnerability to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage. Under any other moon, it gains no extra traits.

Whenever the [MON] is subjected to bludgeoning damage, it takes no damage, and instead is pushed up to [#] ft away from the source of the bludgeoning damage. If the [MON] is subjected to bludgeoning damage while attached to a creature, the [MON] must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or detach from the creature and be pushed [#] ft away.

The [MON] does not age and does not die when it drops to 0 hit points. If the [MON] drops to 0 hit points, it falls into a quiescent state for 25 weeks before returning to activity with full hit points. Its spawned elementals continue fighting whatever hostile creatures attacked the [MON]; if no hostile creatures are present, they defend the [MON]'s area.

The [MON] appears dead in darkness and remains in a passive state until touched by light. When the [MON] sees light, it becomes active and attacks anything that moves. Once active, a [MON] in complete darkness that isn't taking damage returns to its dormant state after [DURATION]. The [MON] poses no threat to creatures passing near it in complete darkness.

The [MON] can spend [DURATION] filling an empty container with a restorative elixir. A creature that drinks the elixir regains [#dX] hit points and its exhaustion is reduced by up to [#] levels. After the elixir has restored a total of [#] hit points or reduced a total of [#] exhaustion levels, the [MON] can't create an elixir in this way again [DURATION].

When the [MON] takes fire damage, it bursts into flame. The [MON] continues burning until it takes cold damage or is immersed in water. A creature that touches the [MON] or hits it with a melee attack while within [#] ft of it while it is burning takes [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage. While burning, the [MON]'s weapon attacks deal an extra [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage.

At the start of each hour, the [MON] can choose to change the precipitation and temperature within 1 mile of it by one stage up or down (no action required). This works like the changing weather conditions aspect of the control weather spell except [MON] can't change wind conditions change immediately and [MON] can never make it warm hot or unbearable heat.

If a creature that breathes air starts its turn in [MON]'s space it must make a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or begin suffocating as its lungs fill with the poisonous air emitted by the [MON]. Suffocation lasts until creature ends its turn in a space not occupied by [MON] or [DURATION]. When the suffocation ends the creature is poisoned [DURATION].

When the [MON] moves, Medium and smaller metal objects that aren't being worn or carried are pulled up to 5 ft closer to the [MON]. If this movement pulls the object into the [MON]'s space, the item sticks to the [MON]. A successful DC [SAVE_DC] Strength check removes a stuck item from the [MON]. Objects made of gold and silver are unaffected by this trait.

A [MON] that has completed a Void henge gains necrotic energy while within 1 mile of the henge. At the start of each of the [MON]'s turns each creature within [#] ft of it must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or take [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage. The [MON] can choose for a creature it is grappling to be immune to the Tainted Auras of all [MON]s.

The master of the [MON] can cast a spell through it, using the [MON]'s senses to target the spell. The range limitations are treated as if the spell originated from the [MON], not the master. The spell effect occurs on the [MON]'s turn, though the master must cast the spell during the master's turn. Concentration spells must still be maintained by the master.

When the [MON] is first brought below half of its maximum hit points, it immediately recharges its breath weapon, if it is not already available. After doing so, the [MON]'s golden scales melt, coating its body in a layer of molten gold. A creature that touches the [MON] or hits it with a melee attack for the first time on a turn takes [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage.

The [MON]'s movement is never impeded by difficult terrain, and its speed can't be reduced by spells or magical effects. It can't be restrained (per the condition), and it escapes automatically from any nonmagical restraints (such as chains, entanglement, or grappling) by spending 5 ft of movement. Being underwater imposes no penalty on its movement or attacks.

Any creature that begins its turn within [#] ft of the [MON] must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] Charisma saving throw or be cursed, losing its resolve in important oaths it has taken. While cursed, creature has disadvantage on [ABILITY] saving throws to maintain concentration and can't add its proficiency bonus to ability checks and saves in which it is proficient.

The [MON] is bound to an amulet. As long as the [MON] and its amulet are on the same plane of existence, the amulet's wearer can telepathically call the [MON] to travel to it, and the [MON] knows the distance and direction to the amulet. If the [MON] is within [#] ft of the amulet's wearer, half of any damage the wearer takes (rounded up) is transferred to the [MON].

When the [MON], dies, it collapses into a pile of ash. Each day the pile of ash is within 1 mile of a holy site of its deity or a worshiper of its deity, it has a 75 percent chance of returning to life, regaining all its hit points and becoming active again. This chance increases to 100 percent if a worshiper of the [MON]'s deity prays over the [MON]'s ashes at dawn.

Over the course of a short rest, a [MON] can form a bond with a rider. Once this bond is formed, the rider suffers no penalties for riding the [MON] without a saddle. Additionally, if an effect forces both the [MON] and its rider to roll a saving throw, the [MON] automatically succeeds if the rider succeeds. If the [MON] bonds with a new rider, the previous bond ends.

A creature that moves within [#] ft of the [MON] for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or be unable to speak a deliberate lie until it starts its turn more than [#] ft away from the [MON]. Affected creatures are aware of this effect, and the [MON] knows whether or not a creature failed on the save.

The [MON] can be commanded to rapidly burn through the remains of its wick, creating a devastating fireball. All creatures within [#] ft of the [MON] must make a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw, taking [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage on a failed save, or half as much damage with a success. The fire spreads around corners. The [MON] is reduced to a lifeless puddle of wax.

The [MON]'s alchemical flame reservoir explodes when the construct is destroyed, spraying nearby creatures with burning fuel. A creature within [#] ft of the [MON] takes [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage, or half as much damage with a successful DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw. This explosion doesn't occur if the [MON] has already fired its alchemical flame jet four times.

A creature who touches the [MON] or hits hits it with an attack while within [#] ft of it must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or take [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage. This acidic matter continues doing [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage at the start of each of the creature's turns until it or an adjacent ally uses an action to wipe off the tears or three rounds elapse.

Any nonmagical slashing or piercing weapon made of metal or wood that hits the swordbreaker the [MON] cracks. After dealing damage, the weapon takes a permanent and cumulative -1 penalty to damage rolls. If its penalty drops to -5, the weapon is destroyed. Nonmagical ammunition made of metal or wood that hits the swordbreaker the [MON] is destroyed after dealing damage.

Any nonmagical weapon made of metal that hits the [MON] corrodes. After dealing damage, the weapon takes a permanent and cumulative -1 penalty to damage rolls. If its penalty drops to -5, the weapon is destroyed. Nonmagical ammunition made of metal that hits the [MON] is destroyed after dealing damage. The [MON] can eat through 2-inch-thick, nonmagical metal in 1 round.

The [MON] has membranes between its fore and hind limbs that expand while falling to slow its rate of descent to [#] ft per round landing on its ft and taking no falling damage. It can move up to 5 ft horizontally for every 1 ft it falls. Can't gain height with its gliding membranes alone. If subject to a strong wind or lift of any kind can use updraft to glide farther.

The [MON] chooses one creature it can see. It moves, acts, and speaks in a macabre imitation of the creature. Its utterances are nonsense, and it can't understand the languages of its chosen target. It maintains this imitation [DURATION]. A creature that hears and sees the [MON] can tell it is performing an imitation with a successful DC [SAVE_DC] Wisdom (Insight) check.

Each creature that starts its turn within [#] ft of the [MON] must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or be unable to correctly judge the distance between itself and its surroundings [DURATION]. An affected creature has disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight, and it can't move more than half its speed on its turn.

A creature who makes eye contact with the [MON] must make a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw. If it rolls a natural 1, it is petrified instantly. Otherwise, on a failure, it is restrained as it begins to petrify. A restrained creature can repeat this saving throw at the end of its next turn, ending the effect on itself on a success, or becoming petrified on a failure.

When the [MON] is hit with a melee attack, the attacker's weapon bes stuck to the web fluid secreted from its scales. If the attacker didn't use a weapon, it must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or be restrained in the webbing. As an action, a creature can make a DC [SAVE_DC] Strength check, escaping or freeing its weapon from the secretions on a success.

A creature that starts its turn within [#] ft of the [MON] must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or feel lethargic [DURATION]. While lethargic, a creature can't use reactions, its speed is halved, and it can't make more than one melee or ranged attack on its turn. In addition, the creature can use either an action or a bonus action on its turn, but not both.

A creature the [MON] can hear can use its action to chastise the [MON], making a Charisma (Intimidation) check. If it does so, the [MON] must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw with a DC equal to the creature's Charisma (Intimidation) check or be frightened of that creature [DURATION]. If the [MON] succeeds on the saving throw, it can't be frightened by that creature [DURATION].

Each day at dawn, the [MON] produces up to 12 vaguely humanoid drones. Drones share a telepathic link with the [MON] and are under its control. A drone uses the statistics of a zombie, except it can't be knocked prone while on the [MON] and can attach itself to the [MON] as a reaction when the [MON] moves. The [MON] can have no more than 12 drones under its control at one time.

Cold air surrounds the [MON]. Small non-magical flames are extinguished in its presence and water begins to freeze. Unprotected characters spending more than [DURATION] within [#] ft of its must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or suffer as if exposed to severe cold. Spells that grant protection from cold damage are targeted by an automatic dispel magic effect.

The [MON] regains [#] hit points at the start of its turn if it is within [#] ft of the duskthorn dryad's vines and it hasn't taken acid or fire damage since its previous turn. The [MON] dies only if it starts its turn with 0 hit points and doesn't regenerate, or if the duskthorn dryad who created it dies, or if the [MON]'s heart inside the dryad's or treant's tree is destroyed.

When reduced to 0 hit points its head and neck separate from body. Snake-like remnant immediately attacks nearest creature moving up to its speed if necessary even if it has already taken its turn this round. This remnant has same stats as original [MON] except it is Medium has [#] hit points and can make only one Bite on its turn. Head remains active [DURATION] or until killed.

When the [MON] takes damage that doesn't kill it, or when it is subjected to fire damage, its magma shell cracks and it is set ablaze. While ablaze, the [MON] sheds bright light for [#] ft and dim light for an additional [#] ft If the [MON] is subjected to cold damage while ablaze, this flame is extinguished. The [MON] can also set itself ablaze or extinguish itself as an action.

The [MON] can't speak with its creator telepathically, but it feels strong emotions and recognizes the objects of those emotions. A creator can telepathically order [MON] to hunt for and attack individuals by sending the [MON] an image of the creature and the appropriate emotion. As long as the [MON] is on such a hunt, it can be more than [#] ft away from its master without wailing.

When the [MON] takes damage from a spell and isn't reduced to 0 hit points, a number of new [MON]s equal to the spell's level appear in unoccupied spaces within [#] ft of the [MON]. If the spell is a cantrip, only one [MON] is created. [#] or more new [MON]s within [#] ft of each other can use their reactions to come together and form a new [MON] in a space within [#] ft of one [MON].

A creature holding the egg containing the [MON]'s soul can use an action to compel the [MON] as if a dominate monster spell were cast on it and the [MON] failed its saving throw. As long as the soul is within the needle, the [MON] can't permanently die. If it is killed, its body reforms in its lair in [DURATION]. If the needle is broken, the [MON] can be killed like any other creature.

When the [MON] is slain, it is reborn in a burst of energy in a [#] ft radius from its body. Roll any die. On an even result, the energy causes plants to grow, and creatures in that area regain [#dX] hit points. On an odd result, creatures in that area must make a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw, taking [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a success.

When the [MON] is reduced to 0 hit points, it disperses into its component kelp in a [#] ft cube. The area is difficult terrain [DURATION]. At the end of that duration, the [MON] reforms, regaining half its hit points and becoming active again. If more than half the kelp that comprises the dispersed [MON] is removed from the water and dried, it can't reform and the creature is destroyed.

The [MON]'s tales have the effect of a lesser restoration spell at will, and once per week it can have the effect of greater restoration. The [MON] designates one listener to benefit from its ability, and that listener must spend [DURATION] listening to its tales. The [MON]s are reluctant to share this benefit and must be bargained with or under the effect of domination to grant the boon.

At the start of the [MON]'s turn, a syringe on its back injects it with an alchemical infusion, which lasts [DURATION]. The [MON] takes [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage when it activates this infusion. The [MON] can breathe poison as an action. In addition, any creature that starts its turn within [#] ft of the [MON] must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or be poisoned [DURATION].

The [MON] can fold itself into a small, almost flat form, perfect for hiding on bookshelves. The [MON] can still be recognized as something other than a book by someone who handles it (doesn't just glance at it on the shelf) and makes a successful DC [SAVE_DC] Intelligence (Nature or Investigation) check. The [MON] can hop or fly (clumsily, by flapping its pages) 5 ft per turn in this form.

If the [MON] sits in a body of slow-flowing or standing water, such as a hot spring or a small creek, for at least [DURATION], the water becomes purified and rendered free of poison and disease. In slow-flowing water, this purification fades [DURATION] after the [MON] leaves the water. In standing water, this purification lasts until a contaminant enters the water while the [MON] isn't in it.

Any creature that starts its turn within [#] ft of the [MON] must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or grow hostile. On its turn, a hostile creature must move to and make one attack against the nearest creature other than the [MON]. If no other creature is near enough to move to and attack, the hostile creature stalks off in a random direction, seeking a target for its hostility.

The [MON]'s undead form is constantly covered with a magical illusion that makes it look like it did in life. This effect is suppressed [DURATION]. The changes wrought by this illusion fail to hold up to physical inspection. Otherwise, a creature must use an action to visually inspect the illusion and succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] Intelligence (Investigation) check to discern the [MON]'s true appearance.

Once on its turn, the [MON] can use half its movement to step into the dreams of a sleeping creature within [#] ft of it. It emerges from the dreams of another sleeper within 1 mile of the first creature, appearing in an unoccupied space within [#] ft of the second. Each sleeper must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or suffer a level of exhaustion as nightmares prevent restful sleep.

The [MON] can store the souls of up to 3 victims inside it at one time. If it has at least 1 soul, a destroyed [MON] gains a new body in [DURATION], regaining all its hit points and becoming active again. The new body appears within [#] ft of its sandy remains. If its sandy remains are soaked with holy water and buried in consecrated ground, its trapped souls are freed, and the [MON] can't rejuvenate.

At the start of the [MON]'s turn, a syringe on its back injects it with an alchemical infusion, which lasts [DURATION]. The [MON] takes [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage when it activates this infusion. The [MON]'s silver hide is covered with salt crystals, increasing its AC by [#]. The [MON]'s melee attacks deal an extra [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage, and the ground within [#] ft of the [MON] becomes difficult terrain.

When immersed in magical darkness, a [MON] emits a brilliant flash of light powerful enough to dispel magical darkness in a [#] ft radius sphere centered on itself, illuminating the area with bright light [DURATION]. Afterwards, the light winks out and the skull falls to the ground, inert. In one week, the [MON] has a 50% chance of becoming active again, though failure to do so means it will never reanimate.

In areas of dim light or darkness, a [MON] is treated as invisible. Artificial illumination, such as a lantern or a light or continual flame spell, does not negate this ability; nothing less than true sunlight or a daylight spell does. The [MON] can't use its speed Surge or its Stygian Breath while invisible. A [MON] can suspend or resume this ability at will, so long as the [MON] is in dim light or darkness.

Any creature that drinks the water of a [MON] or eats fruit from the plants growing in it has a dream (as the spell, save DC [SAVE_DC]) the next time it sleeps. In this dream, the [MON] places a compulsion to carry out some activity as a torrent of images and sensations. When the creature awakens, it is affected by a geas spell (save DC [SAVE_DC], cast as a 7th-level spell) in addition to the effects of dream.

The [MON] is bound to its water source. If the [MON] is separated from its water source for more than [DURATION], the [MON] gains 1 level of exhaustion. It gains an additional level of exhaustion every [DURATION] until it bonds with another water source or [DURATION]. The [MON] can bond with a new water source and remove its levels of exhaustion by finishing a long rest while submerged in the new water source.

When making an opportunity attack, the [MON] can cast a spell with a casting time of 1 action instead of making a weapon attack. If this spell requires a ranged attack roll, the [MON] doesn't have disadvantage on the attack roll from being within [#] ft of a hostile creature, though it may still have disadvantage from other sources. This spell must only target the creature that provoked the opportunity attack.

When the [MON] is first brought below half of its maximum hit points, it immediately recharges its breath weapon, if it is not already available. Its inner flame erupts, burning brightly in its eyes and mouth. After taking damage from its Searing Heat ability, a creature with resistance to fire damage loses it, and a creature with immunity to fire damage reduces it to resistance. Either effect lasts [DURATION].

When the [MON] has [#] hit points or fewer, the spirit within it tears free and tendrils of necrotic energy erupt from its skin. When it hits with any weapon, the weapon deals an extra [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage. When it has [#] hit points or fewer, its weapon attacks instead deal an extra [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage. When it has [#] hit points or fewer, its weapon attacks instead deal an extra [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage.

When three [MON]s are within [#] ft of each other, they can work together to cast communal spells that are more powerful than they could cast individually. To do this, one uses an action to cast a spell, and the other two must use their reactions to complete it. These communal spells are cast at 11th level and have a spell save DC of 13: At will: hold person 3/day: fear, sleep 1/day: confusion, hypnotic pattern.

The [MON]'s horn can be attacked and severed or destroyed, whichever the attacker chooses (AC [#]; [#] hit points; immunity to bludgeoning, poison, and psychic damage). If its horn is severed, the [MON] loses its flying speed, loses [#dX] hit points at the start of each of its turns, and goes into a frenzy. While in a frenzy, the [MON] has advantage on bite attack rolls and attack rolls against it have advantage.

The [MON] must stay at least 5 ft away from a brandished holy symbol or a burning sprig of wolf's bane, and it can't touch or make melee attacks against a creature holding one of these items. After 1 round, the [MON] can make a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw at the start of each of its turns; if the save succeeds, the [MON] temporarily overcomes its superstition and these restrictions are lifted [DURATION].

At the start of each of the [MON]'s turns, each creature grappled by it must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or gain 1 level of exhaustion. If a creature's saving throw is successful or the effect ends for it, the creature is immune to this effect [DURATION] (but any levels of exhaustion already gained remain in effect). For every level of exhaustion drained, the [MON] gains 5 temporary hit points.

Any nonmagical weapon that hits the [MON] is slowly dismantled by the minute constructs that make up the [MON]. After dealing damage, the weapon takes a permanent and cumulative -1 penalty to damage rolls. If its penalty drops to -5, the weapon is destroyed. Nonmagical ammunition that hits the [MON] is destroyed after dealing damage. At the start of each of its turns, the [MON] can choose whether this trait is active.

The [MON] can spend [DURATION] focusing on a creature against which it has sworn vengeance. If the creature is dead or on another plane of existence, it learns that. Otherwise, after focusing, it knows the distance and direction to that creature, and so long as its moving in pursuit of that creature, it ignores difficult terrain. This effect ends if the [MON] takes damage or ends its turn without moving for any reason.

The [MON] can communicate with spawns of The [MON] and all vermin and insects, including swarms and giant varieties, within [#] ft of it via pheromone transmission. In a hive, this range extends to cover the entire hive. This is a silent and instantaneous mode of communication that only [MON], spawn of the [MON], insects, and vermin can understand. All these creatures follow [MON]'s orders and will never harm the devil.

The [MON] can take [DURATION] to perform a cleansing ritual on a creature object or an area within [#] ft of it that is no larger than a [#] ft cube. The affected creature or object is hidden from divination magic [DURATION] as if it was under the effects of the nondetection spell. In an area that is ritually cleansed, divination spells of level [#] or lower don't function and creatures within that area can't be scried.

The [MON] is surrounded at all times by four Medium swarms of Tiny rootlets that move as the [MON] directs. Each swarm has a speed of [#] ft, can be targeted independently, has [#] hit points, and vulnerable to fire damage. Other than that, they have the same statistics as the [MON]'s main body. For each swarm that drops to 0 hit points, the [MON] loses one of its Entrap attacks. A destroyed swarm regrows in [DURATION].

The [MON] is surrounded by a whirling nimbus of tiny motes of starlight. A sighted creature that starts its turn within [#] ft of the [MON] must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or be incapacitated. At the start of a character's turn, a character can choose to avert its eyes and gain immunity against this effect [DURATION], but it must treat the [MON] as invisible while the character's eyes are averted.

Any nonmagical weapon made of metal or wood that hits the [MON] is coated in a corrosive red slime. After dealing damage, the weapon takes a permanent and cumulative -1 penalty to damage rolls. If its penalty drops to -5, the weapon is destroyed. Nonmagical ammunition made of metal or wood that hits the [MON] is destroyed after dealing damage. The [MON] can eat through 2-inch-thick, nonmagical wood or metal in [DURATION].

The [MON] can serve another creature as a familiar, forming a telepathic bond with its willing master. While the two are bonded, the master can sense what the [MON] senses as long as they are within 1 mile of each other. While the [MON] is within [#] ft of its master, the master shares the [MON]'s Magic Resistance trait. At any time and for any reason, the [MON] can end its service as a familiar, ending the telepathic bond.

The [MON] can pinpoint the location of magical items within [#] ft of it. If the [MON] starts its turn within [#] ft of a magic item, it moves to that magic item and hovers around it. If the item is being worn or carried by a creature, the [MON] attacks that creature. If multiple magic items are within [#] ft of the [MON], it moves to the item that is most rare. If more than one item is most rare, choose randomly among them.

Three ghostly spirits haunt the [MON]. The spirits are incorporeal, remain within [#] ft of the [MON] at all times, and can't take actions. Each uses the [MON]'s AC and saving throws, has [#] hit points, can't be turned, and can only be harmed by radiant damage. If an ancestral spirit is reduced to 0 hit points, it disappears, and the [MON]'s AC is reduced by [#]. Dispersed spirits reappear when the [MON] finishes a long rest.

At the start of each of the [MON]'s turns, the [MON] gains one of the following benefits [DURATION]: (1) Darkvision out to a range of [#] ft. (2) A climbing, flying, or swimming speed of [#] ft. (3) Advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on hearing or smell. (4) Bony spikes sprout along its skin and a creature that touches the [MON] or hits it with melee attack while within [#] ft of it takes [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage.

Whenever the [MON] starts its turn with [#] hit points or fewer, roll a d6. On a 6, the [MON] goes berserk. On each of its turns while berserk, the [MON] attacks the nearest creature it can see. If no creature is near enough to move to and attack, the [MON] attacks an object, with preference for an object smaller than itself. Once the [MON] goes berserk, it continues to do so until it is destroyed or regains all its hit points.

The [MON]'s skeletal form is covered with a magical illusion that makes it look like a living willow tree. The [MON] can use a bonus action to dismiss this illusion [DURATION]. The changes wrought by this illusion fail to hold up to physical inspection. Otherwise, a creature must use an action to visually inspect the illusion and succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] Intelligence (Investigation) check to discern the [MON]'s true appearance.

A creature that touches the [MON] or hits it with a melee attack using a metal weapon must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or attract lightning [DURATION]. For the duration, attacks that cause lightning damage have advantage against this creature, the creature has disadvantage on saving throws against lightning damage and lightning effects, and if the creature takes lightning damage, it is paralyzed [DURATION].

When a [MON] is summoned, it creates a mental link between itself and its conjurer. If the [MON]'s assigned target (see Find The target ability, below) dies before the [MON] can drain the target's soul, or if the [MON] is defeated by its target (but not slain), it returns to its conjurer at full speed and attacks. While the [MON] and the conjurer share the same plane, it can use its Find The target ability to locate its conjurer.

When a [MON] dies, it explodes in a surge of partially-digested magical energy. Each creature within [#] ft of it per Feed score must make a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw, taking [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage per Feed score on a failed save, or half as much damage on a success. [DURATION] afterward, the affected area is awash with volatile magic. A creature that starts its turn in the affected area takes [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage.

The [MON] can mimic the calls and voices of any creature it has heard. To use this ability, the [MON] makes a Charisma (Deception) check. Listeners who succeed on an opposed Wisdom (Insight) or Intelligence (Nature) (DM's choice) check realize that something is mimicking the sound. The [MON] has advantage on the check if it is mimicking a general type of creature (a crow's call, a bear's roar) and not a specific individual's voice.

When a creature on the Material Plane touches the [MON] or hits it with a melee attack, the creature is transported to the Ethereal Plane. The creature can see and hear into both the Ethereal and Material Plane but is unaffected by creatures and objects on the Material Plane. It can be seen as a ghostly form by creatures on the Material Plane. It can move in any direction, with each ft of movement up or down costing 2 ft of movement.

Instead of moving, the [MON]'s humanoid form collapses into loose sand and immediately reforms at another unoccupied space within [#] ft of it. This movement doesn't provoke opportunity attacks. After using this trait in sand terrain, the [MON] can Hide as part of this movement even if under direct observation. The [MON] can sand step under doors or through similar obstacles, provided there's a gap large enough for sand to sift through.

The [MON] gains its ability to fly from its magical horn. The horn can be severed from a living [MON], but doing so drives it into a panicked rage as it attempts to slay all those around it. Strangely, [MON]s never use their horns in combat, possibly in fear of accidentally breaking them. A [MON]'s horn is commonly used in the creation of magic items that grant flight, and [MON]s are often the target of hunters seeking to turn a profit.

If the [MON] is reduced to 0 hit points, it stops functioning and becomes inert. [DURATION], if a Small or larger creature that isn't a Construct or undead dies within [#] ft of the deactivated the [MON], a portion of creature's soul is absorbed by the [MON], and it reactivates, regaining all its hit points plus temporary hit points equal to the dead creature's CR. If it remains inert [DURATION], it is destroyed and can't be reactivated.

When a creature hits the [MON] with a bludgeoning or piercing weapon, the creature must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or the weapon becomes stuck to the [MON]. A stuck weapon can't be used. A creature within reach of the [MON] can free one stuck weapon by succeeding on a DC [SAVE_DC] Strength check as an action. Splashing the [MON] with a gallon of alcohol suppresses this trait [DURATION] and frees all stuck weapons.

When the [MON] attacks, it shapes the wind into a simple or martial weapon, which always deals [#dX] magical damage of the same type as that weapon before disappearing. An air weapon shaped like a ranged weapon uses the range of that weapon, except the [MON] doesn't have disadvantage on ranged attack rolls when attacking a target beyond that weapon's normal range. Air weapons don't benefit from any other properties of weapons they mimic.

A creature with exposed bones that touches the [MON] or hits it with a melee attack while within [#] ft of it takes [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage. Any nonmagical weapon made of bone that hits the [MON] corrodes. After dealing damage, the weapon takes a permanent and cumulative -1 penalty to damage rolls. If its penalty drops to -5, the weapon is destroyed. Nonmagical ammunition made of bone that hits the [MON] is destroyed after dealing damage.

The [MON] emits a swirl of cold wind in a [#] ft radius around it. Each creature that enters this area for first time on a turn or starts its turn there must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or be knocked prone. The wind is nonmagical and disperses gas or vapor. At the start of each of its turns, the [MON] chooses whether this effect is active. While it is active, the [MON] has disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks.

It takes a successful DC [SAVE_DC] Wisdom (Perception) check to spot the [MON]'s web. A creature that fails to notice a web and comes into contact with it is restrained by the web. A restrained creature can pull free from the web by using an action and making a successful DC [SAVE_DC] Strength check. The web can be attacked and destroyed (AC [#]; [#] hit points; vulnerable to fire damage; immune to bludgeoning, poison, and psychic damage).

The [MON] is bound to serve another creature as its master. The [MON] obeys all the master's commands, and the master can communicate telepathically with the [MON] as long as they are on the same plane. A dispel evil and good spell's break enchantment option that targets a [MON] can force it to make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, the [MON]'s bond with its master is broken, and it returns to its true form (use human guard statistics).

When the [MON] takes fire damage catches fire taking [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage at the start of each of its turns. Burns until it takes cold or is immersed in water. Creature that touches [MON] or hits it with melee attack while within [#] ft of it while it is burning takes [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage. While burning deals extra [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage on each melee attack and deals [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage to a captured creature at the start of its turn.

Whenever a [MON] drains life force from victims with Gravedust, it can use that energy transform its shape into a more solid form and maintain it. The new form is Small and semi-transparent but roughly the shape of a normal [MON]. In this form, the [MON] isn't amorphous and can't form a whirlwind, but it can speak normally and manipulate objects. The altered form lasts [DURATION] for every point of necrotic damage it delivered against living foes.

The [MON] constantly emits a thick, nonflammable, yellowish oil. When the [MON] is underwater, this oil makes the water within [#] ft of the [MON] difficult terrain. Each time a creature moves more than [#] ft through this area it must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or be restrained by the thick oil [DURATION]. A creature under the effects of a freedom of movement spell or similar magic is immune to the effects of the [MON] Oil.

Once on its turn, the [MON] can use half of its movement to step into the dreams of a sleeping creature within [#] ft of it. It emerges from the dreams of another sleeper within 1 mile of the first creature, appearing in an unoccupied space within [#] ft of the second. If there is no other sleeping creature within range when it uses this ability, the [MON] is ejected into an unoccupied space within [#] ft of the first sleeper and stunned [DURATION].

The [MON] can exist outside of lava for up to [DURATION] each day. If it remains outside of lava [DURATION] or longer, its skin begins to dry and harden like rapidly-cooled magma. While its skin is hardened, it has a walking speed of [#] ft, an AC of [#], and vulnerability to cold damage. If it remains outside of lava [DURATION] or longer, it becomes petrified, transforming into basalt. Its body returns to normal if it is submerged in lava [DURATION].

All elements of a [MON] within 50 miles of their main body constantly communicate with each other. If one is aware of a particular danger, they all are. Any [MON] with at least [#] hit points forms a hive mind, giving it an Intelligence of 14. Below this hit points threshold, it becomes mindless (Intelligence 0) and loses its innate spellcasting ability. At 0 hit points, a few surviving sets of bones scatter, and must spend months to create a new [MON].

The [MON] abhors combat and flees from it if possible. If unable to flee, the [MON] can attack a foe or obstacle to clear a path to safety. As an action, a driver or handler mounted on the [MON] or adjacent to it can attempt a DC [SAVE_DC] Wisdom (Animal Handling) check. On a success, the [MON] moves and attacks as directed by the driver. On a failure, the [MON] flees. The driver or handler must have proficiency in Animal Handling to attempt this check.

The [MON] exists upon the Material Plane in one of two forms and can switch between them at will. In its material form, it has resistance to damage from nonmagical attacks. In its ethereal form, it is immune to damage from nonmagical attacks. The creature's ethereal form appears as a dark purple outline of its material form, with a blackish-purple haze within. In ethereal form, it can move through air as though it were water, with a fly speed of [#] ft.

A tendril on the [MON]'s head sheds bright light in [#] ft radius and dim light extra [#] ft. When creature that can see the light starts its turn within [#] ft of the [MON], it must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or be charmed [DURATION], regarding the [MON] as friendly acquaintance. If the [MON] or one of its allies harms the charmed creature, this effect ends. At the start of its turn the [MON] chooses whether this light is active.

The [MON] can imbue a nonmagical ring with a spell that has a range of self or touch. Doing so expends components as if the [MON] had cast the spell normally and uses a spell slot one level higher than the spell normally requires. When the wearer of the ring activates the ring as an action, the spell is cast as if the [MON] had cast the spell. The [MON] does not regain the spell slot until the ring is discharged or the [MON] chooses to dismiss the spell.

When the [MON] starts its turn within [#] ft of a source of light light is reduced while [MON] remains within [#] ft of light source. Bright light becomes dim and dim becomes darkness. If the [MON] reduces light source's light to darkness [MON] sheds multicolored bright light in [#] ft radius and dim light for additional [#] ft [DURATION] and light source is extinguished if it is nonmagical flame or dispelled if it was created by 2nd level or lower spell.

Any nonmagical weapon made of metal or wood that hits the [MON] corrodes after dealing damage, taking a permanent and cumulative -1 penalty to damage rolls. If this penalty drops to -5, the weapon is destroyed. Nonmagical ammunition made of metal or wood that hits the [MON] is destroyed after dealing damage. Any other metal or organic object that touches it takes [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage. The [MON] can eat through 2-inch-thick, nonmagical wood or metal in 1 round.

A creature that can hear the [MON]'s heartbeat and starts its turn within [#] ft of the [MON] must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or be charmed [DURATION]. Unless surprised, a creature can plug its ears to avoid the saving throw at the start of its turn. If the creature does so, it is deafened until it unplugs its ears. If the creature unplugs its ears while still within range of the [MON]'s heartbeat, it must immediately make the saving throw.

If a [MON] hasn't fed on a Medium-sized or larger creature within the last [DURATION], it is starving. While starving, the [MON]'s AC is reduced by 2, it has advantage on melee attack rolls against any creature that doesn't have all of its hit points, and will direct its attacks at a single foe regardless of tactical consequences. Once it feeds on a Medium-sized or larger corpse or brings a Medium-sized or larger creature to 0 hit points, it is no longer starving.

If a creature with Intelligence 5 or higher eats a bite of the fruit of the [MON], it must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or be knocked prone, becoming incapacitated by fits of laughter as it perceives everything as hilariously funny [DURATION]. An affected creature can repeat this saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. If the target takes damage while prone, it has advantage on the saving throw.

Some the [MON]s can veil themselves in illusion to pass as other similarly shaped creatures. Such the [MON]s can innately cast the disguise self spell at will, often with a longer duration than is normal for that spell. Mightier the [MON]s can cast the true polymorph spell one to three times per day, possibly with a longer duration than normal. Such the [MON]s can change only their own shape, but a rare few can use the spell on other creatures and objects as well.

When a goblin [MON] is slain,whichever goblin killed them will suddenly transforminto a new goblin [MON] (or queen), their stats replacedwith the [MON]'s stats. All surrounding goblinsare inclined thereafter to obey the new goblin [MON].If a goblin [MON] is slain by a non-goblinoid creature,whichever goblin volunteers for the position first isthe one transformed. Goblins are extremely hesitantto do such a thing, as responsibility and stewardshipare such hard work.

The [MON] generates a field of psychic distortion around itself. Each creature that starts its turn within [#] ft of the [MON] must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or lose its ability to speak coherently. A creature that attempts to cast a spell with verbal components after failing this saving throw expends a spell slot but is unable to complete the casting, instead taking [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage per spell level of the spell it attempted to cast.

A [MON] touching the skin of a warm-blooded creature inflicts [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage per hour of contact, and the victim's maximum hit points are reduced by the same number. Blood is drained so slowly that the victim doesn't notice the damage unless it breaks contact with the [MON] (sets it down or hands it to someone else, for example). When contact is broken, the victim notices blood on its skin or clothes with a successful DC [SAVE_DC] Wisdom (Perception) check.

Corpse-black [MON] can see the face of any creature holding or carrying any item the [MON] ever claimed as its own. It also detects the direction and distance to items it ever owned, so long as that item is currently owned by another. If the item changes hands, the new owner becomes the target of the [MON]'s hunt. Bone-white [MON] see individuals who have offended them. Neither time nor distance affects these abilities, so long as both parties are on the same plane.

At the start of each of the [MON]'s turns, each creature within [#] ft of it must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or have disadvantage on its next attack roll or ability check as the moisture within it becomes diseased. If a creature spends at least [DURATION] in the [MON]'s aura or drinks water within the aura, it must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or contract [DISEASE]. Creatures immune to the poisoned condition are unaffected.

When the [MON] reduces a creature to 0 hit points nearby plants erupt with growth. Plants within [#] ft of the body become thick overgrown difficult terrain and all plants within a 2-mile radius centered on the point where the creature was killed become enriched [DURATION] for each CR of the slain creature (minimum of [DURATION]) cumulatively increasing in duration each time the [MON] kills a creature. Enriched plants yield twice the normal amount of food when harvested.

The [MON] emits a [#] ft radius of magical darkness at all times, moving with it and spreading around corners. Darkvision can't penetrate this darkness, and no natural light can illuminate it. If any of the darkness overlaps with an area of light created by a spell of 3rd level or lower, the spell creating the light is dispelled. A successful dispel magic (DC [SAVE_DC]) cast on the [MON] suppresses this aura [DURATION] or until the [MON] reduces a creature to 0 hit points.

When the [MON] dies, all curses currently inflicted by the [MON] be permanent and can be removed only by the remove curse spell or other magic. In addition, the creature that dealt the killing blow must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or be cursed with every option listed in the [MON]'s beak attack. A creature casting remove curse on a creature cursed in this way must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or suffer the curses it just removed.
A beast or humanoid that ends its turn within [#] ft of the [MON] and can see or hear it must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or be charmed [DURATION].

The [MON]'s presence interferes with nonmagical objects within [#] ft of it that have moving parts. Objects that aren't being worn or carried malfunction while within the aura, and, if in the aura [DURATION], they cease to function until repaired. If a creature in the aura uses a nonmagical object with moving parts, roll a d6. On a 1-3, the object malfunctions. A creature can take its action to fix the malfunctioning object by succeeding on a DC [SAVE_DC] Intelligence check.

The spirits that make up the [MON] are bound to a 10 ft by-10 ft panel of wall, behind which their original bodies are trapped. The [MON] can move to nearby walls with its Wall Hop trait, but it can never be more than [#] ft away from its bound wall. If its bound wall is damaged while the [MON] is elsewhere, the [MON] takes half as much damage dealt to the bound wall. When the [MON] finishes a long rest while inhabiting its bound wall, any damage to the bound wall is repaired.

Any normal fire in the [MON]'s space at the end of the [MON]'s turn is extinguished. Magically conjured fire is extinguished if the [MON] succeeds on a DC [SAVE_DC] Constitution check. Only the [MON]'s space is affected; fires larger than the [MON] continue burning outside the [MON]'s space. [DURATION] after the [MON] consumes any flame, its bite attack deals an extra [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage, and any creature that ends its turn in the [MON]'s space takes [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage.

The [MON] has a bowl-like indentation on its head which holds water from the river or lake where it lives. If the [MON]'s head bowl is empty, it has disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks until the bowl is refilled with water. Normal movement and combat do not cause water to spill from the bowl, but an opponent can empty the bowl by knocking the [MON] prone or by making two successful grapple attacks one to grab the [MON], and one to tip its head while it is grappled.

feature.ability_tags: Coating, Ongoing Damage, Spawning, Speed Change
feature.desc: A creature covered in the [MON]'s tar has its speed halved [DURATION]. In addition, the tar ignites if touched by a source of fire or if a creature covered with tar takes fire damage. The tar burns until a creature uses an action to snuff out the flames. A creature that starts its turn covered with burning tar takes [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage. A humanoid that dies while covered in tar rises [DURATION] later as tar ghoul, unless the humanoid is restored to life or its body is destroyed.

If the staff controlling the [MON] is broken or is not being worn or carried by a humanoid, the [MON] goes berserk. On each of its turns while berserk, the [MON] attacks the nearest creature it can see. If no creature is near enough to move to and attack, the [MON] attacks an object with preference for an object smaller than itself. Once the [MON] goes berserk, it continues to do so until it is destroyed, until a new staff is created, or until the staff is worn or carried by a humanoid.

The [MON] is the psychic nexus for every [MON] in its hive. It is aware of the direction and distance to all members of the hive, can telepathically communicate with them when they are within 20 miles, and can sense what they sense when they are within 1 mile of it. The [MON] from its hive that travel more than 20 miles away instinctively know the direction and distance to the hive and try to return. The [MON]s sometimes dispatch rescue missions to recover separated members of the hive.

The [MON] must soak its cap in the blood of a humanoid killed no more than [DURATION] ago at least once every [DURATION]. If it goes more than [DURATION] without doing so, the blood on its cap dries and the [MON] gains one level of exhaustion every [DURATION]. While the cap is dry, the [MON] can't remove exhaustion by any means. All levels of exhaustion are removed immediately when the [MON] soaks its cap in fresh blood. A [MON] that dies as a result of this exhaustion crumbles to dust.

An [MON] glides through stone, dirt, or any sort of earth except metal as easily as a fish glides through water. Its burrowing produces no ripple or other sign of its presence and leaves no tunnel or hole unless the [MON] chooses to do so; in that case, it creates a passageway [#] ft wide by [#] ft high. The spell move earth cast on an area containing an earth-gliding [MON] flings the [MON] back [#] ft and stuns it [DURATION] unless it succeeds on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw.

feature.ability_tags: Advantage, Concentration, Damage Reduction, Shapechanging, Speed Change
feature.desc: When flying at high altitude, the [MON] can, after [DURATION] of concentration, discorporate into clouds. In this form, it has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks, its fly speed increases to [#] ft, it is immune to all nonmagical damage, it has resistance to magical damage, and it can't take any actions except Hide. If it takes damage or descends more than [#] ft from where it transformed, it immediately returns to its corporeal form. The [MON] can revert to its true form as an action.

The [MON] can inscribe a spell from a spellbook or scroll onto the parchment wrappings that cover its body as if copying a spell into a spellbook. Alternatively, it can inscribe a spell another spellcaster knows or has prepared onto its body by striking the spellcaster with its Spell-Siphoning Fist (see below). If the [MON] inscribes a spell with its Spell-Siphoning Fist, the inscription is free and happens immediately. The [MON] can use any spell it has inscribed onto its body once per day.

A creature that is not deafened and starts its turn in the [MON]'s space must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or have disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks that use Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma [DURATION].

A successful DC [SAVE_DC] Wisdom (Perception) check must be made to spot the [MON] snare lines, and the check is always made with disadvantage unless the searcher has some means of overcoming the snares' invisibility. A creature that enters a space containing the [MON] snare lines must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or be restrained by the sticky snares (escape DC [SAVE_DC]). This saving throw is made with disadvantage if the creature was unaware of the snare lines' presence.

The [MON] is spiritually linked to a specific area or landmark. The [MON] gains no benefit from a long rest when more than 1 mile away from its linked area. If the [MON] dies, the area it is linked to loses its vital essence until it forms a new [MON], which can take centuries. When a creature first enters an area that has lost its vital essence in this way, they gain a level of fatigue and a level of strife. This fatigue and strife can be removed only by completing a long rest outside the area.

The [MON] creates a draconic visage in an unoccupied space it can see within [#] ft of it. The visage is a glowing, spectral head and neck, resembling a variety of dragon chosen by the [MON], that sheds dim light out to [#] ft. The visage lasts [DURATION]. While it is visible, the [MON] gains immunity to the damage type dealt by the chosen dragon's breath weapon. Additionally, a creature hostile to the [MON] who starts its turn within [#] ft of the visage and who is aware of the visage [OUTCOME].

The sight of potential host bodies so excites the [MON] that it babbles and giggles madly and childishly, driving nearby creatures insane. All sane creatures that the start their turns within [#] ft of the [MON] must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or be affected by confusion (as the spell) [DURATION]. This is a psychic effect. Creatures that successfully save can't be affected by the same [MON]'s babbling [DURATION]. This action can't be taken when the [MON] is using Soul Exchange.

At the start of each of the [MON]'s turns, each creature within [#] ft of it must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or have disadvantage on its next attack roll or ability check as a gnawing thirst distracts it. For each [DURATION] a creature stays in the [MON]'s aura, it gains one level of exhaustion from dehydration. A level of exhaustion is removed if the creature uses an action to drink 1 pint of water. A [MON] is immune to its own Aura of Thirst as well as the auras of other [MON]s.

Each day at sunrise, the [MON] chooses one of the following: (1) Hardened Face. The [MON] chooses either bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage. The [MON] has resistance to the chosen damage type until the next sunrise. (2) Vaunted Peaks. The [MON] has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks until the next sunrise. (3) Rockslider. As a bonus action once before the next sunrise, the [MON] can make the ground within [#] ft of it difficult terrain. This difficult terrain doesn't cost the [MON] extra movement.

The pain caused by the iron plates bolted to its body keep the [MON] on the edge of madness. Whenever the [MON] starts its turn with [#] hit points or fewer, roll a d6. On a 6, the [MON] goes berserk. On each of its turns while berserk, the [MON] attacks the nearest creature it can see. If no creature is near enough to move to and attack, the [MON] attacks an object, with preference for an object smaller than itself. Once the [MON] goes berserk, it continues to do so until it is destroyed or regains all its hit points.

The [MON] block torse it can liquefy and refreeze trapping and preserving creatures. If golem takes [#] fire on a single turn cavity liquefies if frozen. When cavity is frozen creature that touches golem or hits it with melee attack while within [#] ft of it: [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage. When cavity liquefied creature within [#] ft of golem can use action to pull petrified creature out of golem if golem has one inside. Doing so requires successful DC [SAVE_DC] Strength check and creature attempting: [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage.

At the start of each of the [MON]'s turns, roll a die. On an even roll, its body stretches and speeds up as it takes on a darting form. On an odd roll, its body becomes more solid and slows down as it takes on a sluggish form. Its statistics are the same in each form, except for the following changes: While in a Darting form, the [MON]'s AC increases by 2, and its speed is [#] ft; While in a Sluggish form, the [MON] has resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks, and its speed is [#] ft.

The [MON] attunes itself to the threads of the PCs' fates. Ask each player to write down their prediction of how the PC to their left will die, and at what level. Collect the notes without revealing the answers. When one of those PCs dies, reveal the prediction. If the character died in the manner predicted, they fulfill their destiny and are immediately resurrected by the gods as a reward. If they died at or within one level of the prediction, they return to life with some useful insight into the destiny of someone important.

The [MON] has [#] heads. While it has more than one head, the [MON] has advantage on saving throws against being blinded, charmed, deafened, frightened, stunned, and knocked unconscious. Whenever the [MON] takes [#] or more damage in a single turn, one of its heads dies. If all its heads die, the [MON] dies. At the end of its turn, it grows two heads for each of its heads that died since its last turn, unless it has taken [DMG_TYPE] damage since its last turn. The [MON] regains [#] hit points for each head regrown in this way.

When the [MON] is reduced to 0 hit points, it explodes. Each creature within [#] ft of it, except for other [MON]s, must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or take [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage and be pushed back [#] ft. Two duplicate [MON]s appear in the [MON]'s space and the nearest unoccupied space, each with the same statistics as the original [MON], except one size smaller. When a Tiny duplicate of the [MON] is reduced to 0 hit points, it explodes and doesn't duplicate. All duplicates act on the same initiative.

The [MON] can spend [DURATION] coaxing life essence out of willing creature taking only agreed amount of time from creature's max lifetime. Essence appears as rosy mist that rises from mouth nose or skin of creature and snakes into carved crystal vial in the [MON]'s cloak where it takes the form of a crimson liquid. Creature that drinks such a vial gains life stored within it provided the [MON] gave vial willingly. If the [MON] draws all remaining life from creature creature dies and can be returned to life only via wish spell.

When the [MON] strikes a target with a melee attack, in addition to taking normal damage, the target must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or instantly age [#dX] years. A creature that ages this way has disadvantage on attack rolls, ability checks, and saving throws based on Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution until the aging is reversed. A creature that ages beyond its lifespan dies immediately. The aging reverses automatically after [DURATION], or it can be reversed by greater restoration or similar magic.

A humanoid that starts its turn within [#] ft of the [MON] and can see the [MON]'s true form [OUTCOME]. A frightened creature can repeat this saving throw at the end of each of its turns, with disadvantage if the [MON] is within line of sight, ending the effect on itself on a success. Unless the target is surprised or the revelation of the [MON]'s true form is sudden, the target can avert its eyes and avoid making the initial saving throw. [DURATION], a creature that averts its eyes has disadvantage on attack rolls against the [MON].

The [MON]'s spiked tail is segmented and up to three times the length of its body. When the [MON] takes [#] or more damage in a single turn, a segment of its tail is severed. When the first segment is severed, the tail attack's damage type changes from piercing to bludgeoning and deals one die less of damage. When the second segment is severed, the tail attack no longer deals damage, but it can still grapple. When the third segment is severed, the [MON] can't make tail attacks. The tail re-grows at a rate of one segment per long rest.

When a creature starts its turn within [#] ft of the [MON], the creature must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or be unable to take reactions [DURATION]. Additionally, an affected creature must roll a d8 to determine what it does during that turn. (1-4) The creature does nothing. (5-6) The creature takes no action, but uses all its movement to move in a random direction. (7-8) The creature makes one melee attack against randomly determined creature within its reach, or does nothing if no creature is within its reach.

When a [MON]'s confusion spell affects a target, it can elect to use the following d100 table rather than the standard one: (01-10) Inspired: Advantage on attack rolls, ability checks, and saving throws. (11-20) Distracted: Disadvantage on attack rolls, ability checks, and saving throws. (21-50) Incoherent: The target does nothing but babble or scribble incoherent notes on a new idea. (51-75) Obsessed: The target is recipient of Geas to create a quality magical object. (76-100) Suggestible: The target receives a suggestion from the [MON].

The [MON]'s pool emits a sweet fragrance that lures creatures to drink. Creatures that are neither undead nor constructs within [#] ft of it must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] Wisdom saving throw or be compelled to approach the [MON] and drink. The water is cool and refreshing but carries a sleeping poison: any creature (other than undead and constructs) that drinks from it regains [#dX] hit points and recovers from 1 level of exhaustion, but must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw against poison or fall unconscious [DURATION].

When a creature that can see the [MON] starts its turn within [#] ft of the [MON], the [MON] can force it to make a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw if the [MON] isn't incapacitated and can see the creature. On a failure, a creature becomes charmed [DURATION]. Unless surprised, a creature can avert its eyes to avoid the saving throw at the start of its turn. If the creature does so, it can't see the [MON] [DURATION], when it can avert its eyes again. If the creature looks at the [MON] in the meantime, it must immediately make the save.

With at least [DURATION] of work, a [MON] can refine raw materials and create entirely new objects by combining material it has absorbed. For example, it can create a rope from absorbed hemp, clothing from absorbed flax or wool, and a longsword from absorbed metal. A [MON] can create intricate objects like thieves' tools and objects with moving parts with at least [DURATION] of work and twice the requisite raw materials, but it can't create magic items. The quality of objects it creates is commensurate with the quality of the raw materials.

The [MON] is aware of any creature that uses a psychic ability or communicates telepathically within 100 miles of it. As an action, the [MON] can psychically observe a creature, object, or location it is familiar with within 100 miles. While observing a subject in this way, the [MON] can see, hear, and communicate telepathically, but it is blind and deaf in regard to its physical senses and does not require food or water. The [MON] can psychically observe a subject indefinitely and can end this effect and return to its own senses as an action.

If a creature breaks one of the [MON]'s rules of conduct, it becomes enraged. The [MON] has advantage on Charisma (Intimidation) checks and attack rolls against the offending creature. An offending creature that succeeds on a DC [SAVE_DC] Charisma (Persuasion) check can calm the enraged [MON]. If the offending creature has damaged the [MON] in the last [DURATION], it has disadvantage on this check. A creature that succeeds on a DC [SAVE_DC] Intelligence (Investigation) or Wisdom (Insight) check can determine the [MON]'s rules before enraging it.

The [MON] takes up its entire space. Other creatures can enter the space, but a creature that does so is subjected to the [MON]'s Engulf and has disadvantage on the saving throw. Creatures inside the [MON] can be seen but have total cover. A creature within [#] ft of the [MON] can use an action to pull a creature or object out of the [MON]. Doing so requires a successful DC [SAVE_DC] Strength check, and the creature making the attempt takes [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage. The [MON] can hold [#] Large creatures or [#] smaller creatures inside it at a time.

When a creature that can see the eyes of the [MON]'s severed head starts its turn within [#] ft of the [MON], the [MON] can force it to make a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw if the [MON] isn't incapacitated and can see the creature. On a failed save, the creature [OUTCOME]. Unless surprised, a creature can avert its eyes to avoid the saving throw at the start of its turn. If the creature does so, it can't see the [MON] [DURATION], when it can avert its eyes again. If the creature looks at the [MON] in the meantime, it must immediately make the save.

The [MON]'s scales refract light in iridescent cascades that are hypnotic to gaze upon. If the [MON] is in bright light, a creature within [#] ft of it that looks at it must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or be stunned [DURATION]. Unless surprised, a creature can avoid the saving throw by choosing to avert its eyes at the start of its turn. A creature that averts its eyes can't see the [MON] [DURATION], when it can choose to avert its eyes again. If the creature looks at the [MON] in the meantime, it must immediately make the saving throw.

The [MON] has 10 shiny blue-gray tendrils that constantly grab at things in the environment. Each tendril can pick up or hold a Tiny object, such as a coin or piece of jewelry, that isn't being worn or carried. If it uses all 10 of its tendrils, the [MON] can carry a single Small object, such as a backpack. The [MON] can use its tendrils to interact with objects, but it can't use them to wield a weapon. It has advantage on Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) checks when using its tendrils and can use its tendrils to disarm opponents (see the Disarming Tendrils reaction).

When a creature that can see the [MON] starts its turn within [#] ft of it, the [MON] can force it to make a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw if the [MON] isn't incapacitated and can see the creature. Creature that fails is incapacitated and its speed is reduced to 0 [DURATION] as it remains transfixed in place by the lights. Unless surprised creature can avert its eyes to avoid the save at the start of its turn. If creature does so it can't see the [MON] [DURATION] when it can avert again. If creature looks at [MON] in the meantime it must immediately save.

While in bright light, the [MON]'s carapace shines and glitters. When a creature that can see the [MON] starts its turn within [#] ft of the [MON], the [MON] can force the creature to make a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw if the [MON] isn't incapacitated. On a failure, the creature is blinded [DURATION]. Unless surprised, a creature can avert its eyes to avoid the saving throw at the start of its turn. If it does so, it can't see the [MON] [DURATION], when it can avert its eyes again. If it looks at the [MON] in the meantime, it must immediately make the save.

At the end of each long rest, the [MON] chooses one form of artistic expression, such as song, poetry, dance, fashion, paint, or similar. Until it finishes a long rest, the [MON] has immunity to one type of damage, which is associated with its artistic expression. For example, a [MON] expressing art through song or poetry has immunity to thunder damage, a [MON] expressing art through fashion has immunity to slashing damage, and a [MON] expressing art through paint has immunity to acid damage. This trait can't give the [MON] immunity to force, psychic, or radiant damage.

While attached to a living host, a [MON] leaks negative energy into the host's bloodstream, quickly closing over the creature's wounds with scabrous, necrotic flesh. If the host doesn't already have regeneration, it regains 2 hit points at the start of its turn if it has at least 1 hit point. Track how many "necrotic hit points" a host recovers via Necrotic Regeneration. Magical healing reverses the necrosis and subtracts an equal number of necrotic hit points from those accumulated. When the necrotic hit points equal the host's hit point max, the host becomes a zombie.

When the [MON] dies, its body crumbles into smoldering coals, releasing a great plume of smoke that fills a [#] ft radius sphere centered on the corpse, spreading around corners. The area is heavily obscured and becomes difficult terrain. When a creature enters this area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, it must make a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw, taking [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a success. The smoke lasts [DURATION] or until a wind of moderate or greater speed (at least 10 miles per hour) disperses it.

The [MON] can act as a swarm (composed of smaller elements), or it can grant a single member (called an exarch) control, acting as a singular creature. Changing between forms takes one action. In its singular form, the [MON] can't occupy the same space as another creature, but it can perform sneak attacks and cast spells. In swarm form, the [MON] can occupy another creature's space and vice versa, and it can move through openings at least 1 ft square. It can't change to singular form while it occupies the same space as another creature. It uses its skills normally in either form.

feature.ability_tags: Infecting, Infection Effect, Ongoing Damage, Poisoning
feature.desc: The [MON] produces parasitic worms in its cheeks and it expels these worms into other creatures when it attacks. Worm burrows into target's flesh and that creature is poisoned while infested with at least one worm. At the start of each of infested creature's turns it takes [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage. Any creature can use an action to remove one worm with successful DC [SAVE_DC] Wisdom (Medicine) check. An effect that cures disease removes and kills one worm infesting the creature. When [MON] dies all worms currently infesting creatures die ending infestation in all infested creatures.

While submerged in water its ichor taints water within [#] ft of it. When a creature enters area for the 1st time on a turn or starts its turn there that creature must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or be poisoned while it remains in that area and [DURATION] after it leaves. A poisoned creature that is no longer in the water can repeat this saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. If purify food and drink spell is cast on a space within [#] ft of the [MON] or on space it occupies trait ceases to function [DURATION].

When a creature that can see the [MON]'s eyes starts its turn within [#] ft of the [MON], it can force the creature to make a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw if the [MON] isn't incapacitated and can see the creature. On a failure, the creature is stunned [DURATION]. On a success, the creature is restrained. Unless surprised, a creature can avert its eyes to avoid the saving throw at the start of its turn. If the creature does so, it can't see the angel [DURATION], when it can avert its eyes again. If the creature looks at the angel in the meantime, it must immediately make the save.

When a humanoid that can see the [MON] starts its turn within [#] ft of it, it [OUTCOME]. A frightened creature can repeat this saving throw at the end of each of its turns, with disadvantage if the [MON] is within line of sight, ending the effect on itself on a success. Unless it is surprised, a creature can avert its eyes to avoid save at the start of its turn. If it does so, it can't see the [MON] [DURATION]. If it looks at [MON] in the meantime, it must immediately make this saving throw. If the [MON] sees itself reflected on a polished surface, it is affected by its own Memory of Shame.

When a creature that can see the [MON] starts its turn within [#] ft of the [MON], the [MON] can force it to make a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw if the [MON] isn't incapacitated and can see the creature. On a failure, a creature is incapacitated and its speed is reduced to 0 as it is mesmerized by the [MON]. Unless surprised, a creature can avert its eyes to avoid the saving throw at the start of its turn. If the creature does so, it can't see the [MON] [DURATION], when it can avert its eyes again. If the creature looks at the [MON] in the meantime, it must immediately make the save.

[MON]s figure all magic works the same way that magic potions do. As such, they devour spell components, spell scrolls, and magical trinkets alike when they are made aware of them. The [MON]s instinctively know which creatures have magic items on them. When they successfully grab a creature, they use their next action to take that creature's nearest magic item and then stuff it down their throats. If it is a weapon, it deals damage to them as if they had been hit by that weapon. If it is a piece of armor, their mouths stretch to fit around it. They are now imbued with the powers of the devoured magic item.

The [MON] radiates a psychic aura in a [#] ft radius that causes creatures to doubt intentions of their friends. When a creature enters this area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, it must make a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw. On a failure, any beneficial spell (such as bless or heroism) cast by that creature, including spells already in effect, can't affect its allies or ally while it remains in the aura. In addition, that creature can't take the Help action or accept assistance from a ally, including assistance from spells such as bless or cure wounds, while it remains in aura.

The [MON] can either use an action or move up to its speed each turn, not both. The [MON] can hold up to three Small operators. If it has at least one operator, it can move and act normally as long as the operator spends its entire turn operating the [MON]. When it has more than one operator, it has additional traits as long as the additional operators spend their entire turns operating the [MON]. If a creature scores a critical hit against the [MON], the creature can target one of the operators with the attack instead. Otherwise, the operators can't be targeted and are immune to damage while operating the [MON].

When the [MON] is killed it explodes in a swath of celestial destruction. Each creature and object within 1 mile of the [MON] takes [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage, [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage plus [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage.
