Each damage type can be reduced by half with a successful DC [SAVE_DC] saving throw: [ABILITY] against bludgeoning, [ABILITY] against cold, and [ABILITY] against psychic. Additionally, a creature that fails two or three of the saving throws is affected by a plane shift spell and sent to a random plane. If it is sent to the plane it currently occupies, it appears 5d100 miles away in a random direction.

When a creature with an Intelligence of 3 or higher that can see the [MON] starts its turn within [#] ft of the [MON], the [MON] can force it to make a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw if the [MON] isn't incapacitated and can see the creature. On a failure, the target takes [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage and is incapacitated [DURATION]. Unless surprised, a creature can avert its eyes to avoid the saving throw at the start of its turn. If the creature does so, it can't see the [MON] [DURATION], when it can avert its eyes again. If the creature looks at the [MON] in the meantime, it must immediately make the saving throw.

When the [MON] is in an area of bright light, a creature within [#] ft of it that looks at it must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or be blinded [DURATION]. Unless it is surprised, a creature can avoid the saving throw by choosing to avert its eyes at the start of its turn. A creature that averts its eyes can't see the [MON] [DURATION], when it can choose to avert its eyes again. If the creature looks at the [MON] in the meantime, it must immediately make the saving throw. The saving throw is made with advantage if the [MON] is in dim light, and this ability has no effect if the [MON] is in darkness.

A creature that touches the [MON] or hits it with a melee attack while within [#] ft of it takes [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage, and must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or the weapon becomes stuck in the [MON]'s body. If the weapon's wielder can't or won't let go of the weapon, the wielder is grappled while the weapon is stuck. While stuck, the weapon can't be used. Until the grapple ends, the wielder takes [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage at the start of each of its turns. To end the grapple, the wielder can release the weapon or pull it free by taking an action to make a DC [SAVE_DC] Strength check and succeeding.

The [MON]'s mouth is a compartment that is [#] ft long, [#] ft wide, and [#] ft high with a single entry and exit. The [MON] can control the ambient pressure, temperature, gravity, moisture, and breathable air levels inside its mouth, allowing creatures and objects within it to exist comfortably in spite of conditions outside the [MON]. Creatures and objects within the [MON] have total cover against attacks and other effects outside the [MON]. As an action, a creature inside the [MON] can interact with the crystalline growths inside the [MON]'s mouth and sense what the [MON] senses, gaining the benefits of its blindsight.

The eldritch magic that powers the [MON] produces a magnetic power that seizes metal objects that touch it, including metal weapons. When a creature successfully strikes the [MON] with a metal melee weapon, the attacker must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or the weapon becomes stuck to the [MON] until the [MON] releases it or is destroyed. The saving throw uses the same ability as the attack used. The [MON] can release all metal weapons stuck to it whenever it wants. A [MON] always drops all weapons stuck to it when it believes it is no longer threatened. This ability affects armor only during a grapple.

When the [MON] takes at least 15 slashing damage at one time, a chunk of its oozing flesh falls off into an unoccupied space within [#] ft of it. This flesh isn't under the [MON]'s control, but it views the [MON] as an ally. The oozing flesh acts on the [MON]'s initiative and has its own action and movement. It has AC [#], [#] hit points, and a walking speed of [#] ft. It can make one attack with a +6 to hit, and it deals [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage on a hit. If not destroyed, the oozing flesh lives for 1 week, voraciously consuming any non-[MON] creature it encounters. After that time, it dissolves into a puddle of water and gore.

When a creature that can see the [MON]'s eye starts its turn within [#] ft of the [MON], the [MON] can force it to make a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw if the [MON] isn't incapacitated and can see the creature. On a failure, the creature takes [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage and is incapacitated [DURATION]. On a success, the creature takes half as much damage only. Unless surprised, a creature can avert its eyes to avoid the saving throw at the start of its turn. If the creature does so, it can't see the [MON] [DURATION], when it can avert its eyes again. If the creature looks at the [MON] in the meantime, it must immediately make the save.

When the [MON] takes fire damage, it catches fire. If the [MON] starts its turn on fire, it takes [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage. The [MON]'s saturated body douses the fire at the end of the [MON]'s turn. Creatures engulfed by the [MON] don't take fire damage from this effect. If the [MON] dies while it is on fire, it explodes in a burst of fire and flaming peat. Each creature within [#] ft of the [MON] must make a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw, taking [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a success. If a creature is engulfed by the [MON] when it dies in this way, the creature has disadvantage on the saving throw.

When a creature that can see the [MON] starts its turn within [#] ft of the [MON], the [MON] can force it to make a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw if the [MON] isn't incapacitated and can see the creature. On a failed save, the creature is incapacitated and its speed is reduced to 0 [DURATION]. A creature that isn't surprised can avert its eyes to avoid the saving throw at the start of its turn. If it does so, it can't see the [MON] [DURATION], when it can avert its eyes again. If it looks at the [MON] in the meantime, it must immediately make the saving throw. Creatures immune to being frightened are immune to the [MON]'s Transfixing Gaze.

When a creature that can see the [MON]'s eyes starts its turn within [#] ft of the [MON], it must make a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw if the [MON] isn't incapacitated and can see the creature. On a failed saving throw, the creature has its pain threshold lowered, so that it becomes vulnerable to all damage types [DURATION]. Unless it is surprised, a creature can avoid the saving throw by averting its eyes at the start of its turn. A creature that averts its eyes can't see the [MON] for one full round, when it chooses anew whether to avert its eyes again. If the creature looks at the [MON] in the meantime, it must immediately make the save.

If a creature mounts the [MON], the creature must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or be paralyzed and restrained by chains on the [MON]'s back until the next dawn. While it has a rider captured in this way, the [MON] takes Dash or Disengage actions on each of its turns to flee with the rider. After it moves [#] ft, it disappears with the captured rider, racing along a nightmarish landscape. At the next dawn, it returns to the space where it disappeared or the nearest unoccupied space, the rider lands in an unoccupied space within [#] ft of the [MON], and [MON] flees. At the end of the ride, the rider gains one level of exhaustion.

A [MON] that's immersed in water or whose boiler is soaked with at least 20 gallons of water (such as from a water elemental) may be stopped in its tracks by the loss of steam pressure in the boiler. In the case of a water elemental, dousing a [MON] destroys the elemental and the [MON] must make a DC [SAVE_DC] Constitution saving throw. If it succeeds, the water instantly evaporates and the [MON] continues functioning normally. If it fails, the [MON]'s fire is extinguished and the boiler loses pressure. The [MON] acts as if affected by a slow spell [DURATION], then becomes paralyzed until its fire is relit and it spends [DURATION] building up pressure.

A creature that touches or deals slashing or piercing damage to a [MON] while within [#] ft of the creature shreds its delicate linen wrappings, releasing a flurry of skittering scarabs. The attacking creature must make a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw to avoid them. On a failure, these beetles flow onto the attacker and deal [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage to it at the start of each of its turns. A creature can remove beetles from itself or from another affected creature within reach by using an action and making a successful DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw. The beetles are also destroyed if the affected creature takes damage from an area effect.

The [MON] babbles incoherently while it can see any creature and isn't incapacitated. Each creature that starts its turn within [#] ft of the [MON] and can hear it must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or be unable to take reactions [DURATION]. An affected creature also rolls a d8 to determine what it does during its turn. On a 1 to 4, the creature does nothing. On a 5 or 6, the creature takes no action or bonus action and uses all its movement to move in a randomly determined direction. On a 7 or 8, the creature must make a melee attack against a randomly determined creature within its reach, or does nothing if it can't make such an attack.

When a creature that can see the [MON] starts its turn within [#] ft of the [MON], the [MON] can force it to make a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw if the [MON] is not incapacitated. On a failed save, the creature [OUTCOME]. If the creature is concentrating on a spell, that creature must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or lose concentration on the spell. Unless surprised, a creature can avert its eyes to avoid the saving throw at the start of its turn. If the creature does so, it can't see the [MON] [DURATION], when it can avert its eyes again. If the creature looks at the [MON] in the meantime, it must immediately make the saving throw.

When a creature that can see the [MON]'s eyes starts its turn within [#] ft of the [MON], the [MON] can force it to make a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw if the [MON] isn't incapacitated and can see the creature. On a failed save, the creature is paralyzed [DURATION]. A creature that isn't surprised can avert its eyes to avoid the saving throw at the start of its turn. If it does so, it can't see the [MON] [DURATION], when it can avert its eyes again. If it looks at the [MON] in the meantime, it must immediately make the save. Canines are immune to the [MON]'s Paralyzing Gaze, and canine-like humanoids, such as werewolves, have advantage on the saving throw.

When a humanoid that can see the [MON]'s eyes starts its turn within [#] ft of the [MON], the [MON] can force it to make a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw if the [MON] isn't incapacitated and can see the creature. If the creature fails, it is charmed [DURATION]. The charmed creature can repeat this saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. Unless surprised, a creature can avert its eyes to avoid the saving throw at the start of its turn. If the creature does so, it can't see the [MON] [DURATION], when it can avert its eyes again. If the creature looks at the [MON] in the meantime, it must immediately make the save.

The [MON] is surrounded in a [#] ft radius by a ferocious storm. The storm imposes disadvantage on ranged weapon attack rolls and Wisdom (Perception) checks based on sight or hearing within that area. The [MON]'s own senses and attacks are not impaired by this trait. The tempest extinguishes open flames and disperses fog. A flying creature in the tempest must land at the end of its turn or fall. Each creature that starts its turn within [#] ft of the [MON] must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or be pushed [#] ft away from the [MON]. Any creature within [#] ft of the [MON] must spend 2 ft of movement for every 1 ft it moves when moving closer to the [MON].

The chaos of combat causes a [MON] to swap between personalities at the start of each of its turns. To determine which spirit is in control, roll a d6: (1) Cautious: The [MON] moves away from hostile creatures if possible and makes ranged attacks or casts spells. (2) Fickle: The [MON] attacks a creature it didn't attack on its last turn. (3) Terrified: The [MON] focuses entirely on escaping from hostile creatures, using its action to Disengage, Dash, or Hide. (4) Bloodthirsty: The [MON] attacks the nearest creature. (5) Hateful: The [MON] attacks the creature with the fewest hit points remaining. (6) Courageous: The [MON] attacks the creature with the most hit points remaining.

When a creature that can see the [MON]'s faces starts its turn within [#] ft of it and the [MON] isn't incapacitated and can see the creature, at least one of the [MON]'s faces shifts to look like one of the creature's departed loved ones or bitter enemies. The target must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or take [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage and be frightened of the [MON] [DURATION]. Unless it is surprised, a creature can avert its eyes to avoid the save at the start of its turn. If a creature does so, it must treat the [MON] as invisible [DURATION], when it can avert again. If a creature looks at the [MON] in the meantime, it must immediately make the saving throw.

During the day a [MON] appears much as it did in life and loses its Incorporeal Movement trait, its Touch of Forgetfulness action, and its immunity to being grappled and restrained. It retains all other statistics. While in this form, it has a Strength score of 10. If attacked in this form, it relies on its spells to defend itself, but it reverts to its undead form as soon as it takes any damage. When the sun sets or when it takes any damage, the [MON] assumes its undead form, and it has all of its listed statistics. Any creature witnessing this transformation [OUTCOME]. A [MON] reverts to its living form in the morning, though creatures witnessing this don't need to make saving throws.

When a creature starts its turn in the [MON]'s space or enters the [MON]'s space for the frist time on a turn, it must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or be blinded as its eyes strain from their sockets. This blindness lasts until the creature ends its turn and isn't in the [MON]'s space. If a creature's saving throw is successful or the effect ends for it, the creature is immune to this effect [DURATION], although it remains blinded until it leaves the [MON]'s space. If a creature is already blinded by Eye Extraction and fails this saving throw again, its eyes are pulled from their sockets to join the [MON], it takes [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage, and it is permanently blinded.

The [MON] makes all attacks, saving throws, and skill checks with advantage when its creator is within [#] ft of its book. The [MON]'s hit point max is reduced by 1 for every [DURATION] it is more than [#] ft from its book. If its book is destroyed or moved to a different plane of existence, the [MON] must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] Constitution saving throw or die. The [MON] can bind itself to new book by spending a short rest in contact with the new book. If its creator dies, the [MON] can be convinced to pass ownership of the book to a new creature if the creature succeeds on a DC [SAVE_DC] Charisma check. The new owner becomes the [MON]'s new "creator" and inherits the [MON] along with the book.

The [MON] can exist outside of lava or magma [DURATION] each day. If it starts its turn outside of lava and hasn't taken fire damage since the end of its previous turn, its shell begins to cool and harden. While its shell is hardened, the [MON] has walking speed of [#] ft, AC [#], and vulnerability to bludgeoning damage. If it starts its turn in lava or if it took fire damage since the end of its previous turn, its shell becomes molten again. If the [MON] remains outside of lava for more than [DURATION], its shell becomes petrified and the [MON] goes into hibernation. Its body returns to normal if it is submerged in lava or magma [DURATION]. The [MON] dies if it remains in hibernation for 100 years.

An invisible magical eye is created under the [MON]'s control, allowing it to watch its territory without leaving the burial mound. The eye travels at the speed of thought and can be up to 5 miles from the [MON]'s location. The [MON] can see and hear as if it were standing at the eye's location, and it can use its innate spellcasting abilities as if it were at the eye's location. The eye can be noticed with a successful DC [SAVE_DC] Wisdom (Perception) check and can be dispelled as if it were 3rd-level spell. Spells that block other scrying spells work against Sepulchral Scrying as well. Unless dismissed by its creator or dispelled, lasts [DURATION] after its creation; only one can be created per day.

The [MON]'s form automatically changes based on the presence of light: Day Form. While more than half of the [MON] is in darkness, it appears as a glowing orb of light but sheds no light. In this form, its attacks deal radiant damage, and it has immunity to radiant damage and vulnerability to necrotic damage. Night Form. While more than half of the [MON] is in bright light, it appears as an orb of darkness. In this form, its attacks deal necrotic damage, and it has immunity to necrotic damage and has vulnerability to radiant damage. Twilight Form. While the [MON] is in dim light, it appears as split orb of light and darkness. Its attacks deal force damage, and it does not have any immunities or resistances.

When a creature that can see the [MON]'s eyes starts its turn within [#] ft of the [MON], the [MON] can force it to make a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw if the [MON] isn't incapacitated and can see the creature. On a failed saving throw, the creature takes [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage, its hit point max is reduced by an amount equal to the acid damage it takes (which ends after a long rest), and it is paralyzed [DURATION]. Unless surprised, a creature can avert its eyes at the start of its turn to avoid the saving throw. If the creature does so, it can't see the [MON] [DURATION], when it chooses again whether to avert its eyes. If the creature looks at the [MON] before then, it must immediately make the saving throw.

When the [MON] casts hallucinatory terrain, the area appears so lush and inviting that those who view it feel compelled to visit. Any creature that approaches within [#] ft of the terrain must make a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw. Those that fail are affected as by the enthrall spell with the [MON] as the caster; they give the mirage their undivided attention, wanting only to explore it, marvel at its beauty, and rest there for an hour. The [MON] can choose to have creatures focus their attention on it instead of the hallucinatory terrain. Creatures affected by the enthrall effect automatically fail saving throws to disbelieve the hallucinatory terrain. This effect ends if the hallucinatory terrain is dispelled.

When a creature that can see the [MON]'s eye starts its turn within [#] ft of the [MON], the creature must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or be disoriented. While disoriented, the creature is knocked prone each time it tries to move or take the Dash or Disengage action. To recover from disorientation, a creature must start its turn outside the [MON]'s gaze and succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw. A creature that isn't surprised can avert its eyes at the start of its turn to avoid the effect. In that case, no saving throw is necessary but the creature treats the [MON] as invisible [DURATION]. If during its turn the creature chooses to look at the [MON], it must immediately make the saving throw.

Whenever the [MON] makes a root attack, it can choose a point on the ground within [#] ft of it. The root bursts from the ground, and that point becomes the attack's point of origin. After attacking, the exposed root protrudes from that point, and the [MON] gains a reaction each turn that it can only use to make an opportunity attack with that root. A root has AC [#], [#] hit points, and resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks. Damaging a root doesn't damage the [MON] tree. The [MON] can have up to 5 roots active at one time. If it makes a root attack while it has 5 roots active, one of the active roots burrows back into the ground and a new root appears at the location of the new attack.

The [MON] becomes incorporeal and appears as a dark gray shadow while any living creature looks directly at it. While incorporeal, it can move through other creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain. It takes [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage if it ends its turn inside an object. While incorporeal, it also gains resistance to acid, fire, lightning, and thunder damage, and bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks. The [MON] has no control over this trait. Unless surprised, a creature can avert its eyes to avoid looking directly at the [MON] at the start of its turn. If the creature does so, it can't see the [MON] [DURATION], when it can avert its eyes again. If a creature looks at the [MON], the [MON] becomes incorporeal.

At the start of each of the [MON]'s turns, each creature within [#] ft of the [MON] must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or the metal items worn or carried by it stick to the [MON]'s shell. A creature that is made of metal or is wearing metal armor that fails the saving throw is stuck to the shell and restrained. If the item is a weapon and the wielder can't or won't let go of the weapon, the wielder is adhered to the shell and is restrained. A stuck item can't be used. A creature can take its action to remove one creature or object from the [MON]'s shell by succeeding on a DC [SAVE_DC] Strength check. Items made of gold and silver are unaffected by the [MON]'s Magnetic Shell. When the [MON] dies, all metal creatures and objects are released.

When a creature that can see the [MON]'s eyes starts its turn within [#] ft of the [MON], the [MON] can force it to make a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw if the [MON] isn't incapacitated and can see the creature. Otherwise, a creature that fails the saving throw begins to turn to stone and is restrained. The restrained creature must repeat this saving throw at the end of its next turn, becoming petrified on a failed save, or ending the effect on itself on a success. The petrification lasts [DURATION]. Unless surprised, a creature can avert its eyes to avoid the saving throw at the start of its turn. If the creature does so, it can't see the [MON] [DURATION], when it can avert is eyes again. If the creature looks at the [MON], it must immediately make the save.

The [MON] can't replenish its spells naturally. Instead, it uses grappled spellcasters as spell reservoirs, draining uncast spells to power its own casting. Whenever the [MON] wishes to cast a spell, it consumes a number of spell slots from its victim equal to the spell slots necessary to cast the spell. If the victim has too few spell slots available, the [MON] can't cast that spell. The [MON] can also draw power from drained spellcasters or creatures without magic ability. It can reduce a grappled creature's Wisdom by [#dX], adding 2 spell slots to its spell reservoir for every point lowered. A creature reduced to 0 Wisdom is unconscious until it regains at least one point, and can't offer any more power. A creature regains all lost Wisdom when it finishes a long rest.

Whenever the [MON] starts its turn with [#] hit points or fewer, roll a d6. On a 6, the [MON] goes berserk. On each of its turns while berserk, the [MON] attacks the nearest creature it can see. If no creature is near enough to move to and attack, the [MON] attacks an object, usually an object smaller than itself. Once the [MON] goes berserk, it continues to attack until it is destroyed or it regains all its hit points. The [MON]'s creator, if within [#] ft of the berserk [MON], can calm it by speaking firmly and persuasively. The [MON] must be able to hear its creator, who must use an action to make a DC [SAVE_DC] Charisma (Persuasion) check. If the check succeeds, the [MON] ceases being berserk. If it takes damage while still at [#] hit points or fewer, the [MON] might go berserk again.

feature.ability_tags: AC Change, Attaching, Damage Reduction, Zero Speed
feature.desc: The [MON] can bond with willing humanoid creature that remains in physical contact with it [DURATION]. While bonded this way host gains +2 bonus to AC and saves and resistance to all damage, and the [MON]'s speed is 0 moving with host when it moves. Each time host takes damage the [MON] takes same amount. If host is subjected to effect that would force it to save host can use its save bonuses or the [MON]'s. If both are subjected to same effect only one is affected the [MON]'s choice. The [MON] and host otherwise retain their own stats and take separate turns. The [MON] and host can't be separated unless the [MON] chooses to terminate connection. The [MON] can detach itself safely from host over course of [DURATION] or can detach itself from creature as an action which immediately kills host.

If a creature starts its turn within [#] ft of the [MON] and the two of them can see each other, the creature must make a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw if the [MON] isn't incapacitated. On a failed save, the creature begins to turn to stone and is restrained. It must repeat this saving throw at the end of its next turn. On a success, the effect ends. On a failure, the creature is petrified [DURATION]. A creature that isn't surprised can avert its eyes to avoid the saving throw at the start of its turn. If it does so, it can't see the [MON] [DURATION], when it can avert its eyes again. If it looks at the [MON] in the meantime, it must immediately make the save. If the [MON] sees its reflection within [#] ft of it in bright light, it mistakes itself for a rival and the targets itself with its gaze.

The [MON] can use its bonus action to shift its purpose between Destructor, Executioner, and Punisher. (1) Destructor: The [MON]'s purpose is to destroy unholy monuments and statues. Its weapon attacks deal double damage to objects and structures. (2) Executioner: The [MON]'s purpose is to slay a specific creature. The [MON] has advantage on attack rolls against a specific creature, chosen by its deity. As long as the [MON] and the victim are on the same plane of existence, the [MON] knows the precise location of the creature. (3) Punisher: The [MON]'s purpose is to punish, but not kill, creatures, inflicting long-term suffering on those of its deity's choosing. A creature reduced to 0 hit points by the [MON] loses [#dX] Charisma as its body is horribly scarred by the deity's retribution. The scars last [DURATION].

If a target is already grappled in a whip at the start of the [MON]'s turn, both creatures make opposed Strength (Athletics) checks. If the grappled creature wins, it takes [#dX] + [DMG_MOD] [DMG_TYPE] damage, and remains grappled. If the [MON] wins, the grappled creature is dragged into the [MON]'s stomach maw, a mass of churning gears, razor teeth, and whirling blades. The creature takes [#dX] + [DMG_MOD] [DMG_TYPE] damage and is grappled, and the whip is free to attack again on the [MON]'s next turn. The creature takes another [#dX] + [DMG_MOD] [DMG_TYPE] damage automatically at the start of each of the [MON]'s turns for as long as it remains grappled in the maw. Only one creature can be grappled in the punishing maw at a time. The [MON] can freely "spit out"a creature or corpse during its turn, to free up the maw for another victim.

When the [MON] regains hit points from its Regeneration gains random teratoma. Teratoma and effects last until removed or replaced by another. The [MON] can have only 3 at a time. If it would gain a 4th oldest fades and is replaced. Teratomas (d6):1 New Senses: A bevy of new ears and noses give [MON] advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on hearing or smell.2 Many Feet: The [MON] can't be knocked prone.3 Adrenal Overdrive: Can't be frightened or suffer exhaustion.4 Clinging Limbs: When this teratoma is removed with Fling Limb action it attaches to target. While attached to target target takes [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage at the start of each of its turns. A creature including target can use its action to detach teratoma.5 Echo Chambers: The [MON] hasblindsight out to a range of [#] ft.6 New Pain Nerves: Disadvantage on any non-attack roll.

The [MON] consists of Huge central spire and 3 Small clusters. Each cluster acts on the [MON]'s turn and shares its move allowing spire and clusters to swim total of [#] ft on the [MON]'s turn. Cluster can't move more than [#] ft from spire. Cluster over [#] ft away from spire for over [DURATION] enters dormant state becoming new the [MON] after [DURATION]. The [MON] and its clusters share hit points and damage dealt to cluster or spire reduces shared total. If more than one section of the [MON] is included the area of a in damaging spell or effect, the [MON] makes one save and takes damage as if only one section was affected. When the [MON] takes [#] damage in one turn cluster is destroyed. At end of its turn if the [MON] took damage on previous turn it can expel one new cluster from spire per [#] damage it took. Can't have more than 5 clusters active at a time.

The [MON] power to grant wishes is legendary among mortals. Only the most potent [MON]s, such as those among the nobility, can do so. A particular [MON] that has this power can grant one to three wishes to a creature that isn't a [MON]. Once a [MON] has granted its limit of wishes, it can't grant wishes again for some amount of time (usually 1 year). and cosmic law dictates that the same [MON] can expend its limit of wishes on a specific creature only once in that creature's existence. To be granted a wish, a creature within [#] ft of the [MON] states a desired effect to it. The [MON] can then cast the wish spell on the creature's behalf to bring about the effect. Depending on the [MON]'s nature, the [MON] might try to pervert the intent of the wish by exploiting the wish's poor wording. The perversion of the wording is usually crafted to be to the [MON]'s benefit.

The [MON] is always accompanied by its past and future selves. They occupy the [MON]'s same space seconds before and after the [MON] and can't be targeted separately. They provide the [MON] with the following benefits. * The [MON] can concentrate on two spells simultaneously. If it casts a third spell that requires concentration, the [MON] loses concentration on the oldest spell. If the [MON] is concentrating on two spells and loses concentration because of taking damage, it loses concentration on the oldest spell. * When a creature targets the [MON] with an attack, roll a d6. On a 1 through 4, the attack hits one of the [MON]'s future or past selves, halving the damage the [MON] takes. On a 5 or 6, the attack hits the [MON], and it takes damage as normal. The [MON] is still the target of the attack and is subject to effects that trigger when a creature is hit or damaged.

A dome of magic covers the [MON] just large enough to contain its shell. The [MON] can control the ambient pressure temperature water levels and breathable air levels (for air-breathing passengers) inside allowing creatures and objects within it to exist comfortably in spite of conditions outside. Creatures and objects within the shell have total cover against attacks and other effects outside the [MON]. Creatures inside the shell can exit whenever they want but nothing can pass into the shell's dome unless the [MON] allows it. Area inside dome is a magnificent palace carved into [MON]'s shell complete with open 'air' balconies used as entrances/exits and numerous covered chambers that can comfortably hold up to 50 passengers. Palace is [#] ft long [#] ft wide and [#] ft tall. When it dies any creatures inside dome are expelled into unoccupied spaces near the closest exit.

By concentrating [DURATION] on a specific object, a [MON] learns more about the object's most recent owner. The effects of this trait are different depending on if the most recent owner is alive or dead. This trait only works once per object. * If the most recent owner is alive, the [MON] sees through that person's eyes [DURATION]. This works like the clairvoyance spell, except the most recent owner is the sensor and controls which direction it is pointed, how far it can see, etc. The most recent owner must make a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw. On a success, it gets the sensation that it is being watched. * If the most recent owner is dead, the [MON] can learn five things about the person's life through dream-like visions and emotions. This works like the speak with dead spell, except the spirit can only answer questions about events in which the object was present.

The [MON] is surrounded by one hundred, magical, spectral mage hands. The hands can't be targeted by spells or attacks and are immune to damage. The hands float within [#] ft of the [MON] and move with it. The [MON] can decide if the hands are visible. Each hand can carry an object weighing up to 10 pounds and no more than three hands can work in tandem to carry one larger object. The [MON]'s Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) checks have a range of [#] ft. Whenever the [MON] makes a Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check, it can make up to four such checks as part of the same action, but each check must be against a different target. The [MON] can perform actions normally restricted to creatures with hands, such as opening a door, stirring a bowl of soup, or carrying a lantern. The [MON] can't wield weapons or shields or make attacks, except as part of the [MON]'s Flying Fists action.

When a creature that can see the [MON]'s eyes starts its turn within [#] ft of the [MON], the [MON] can force it to make a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw if the [MON] isn't incapacitated and can see the creature. Otherwise, a creature that fails the save begins to turn to stone and is restrained. The restrained creature must repeat this saving throw at the end of its next turn, becoming petrified on a failed save, or ending the effect on itself on a success. The petrification lasts [DURATION]. Unless surprised, a creature can avert its eyes to avoid the saving throw at the start of its turn. If the creature does so, it can't see the [MON] [DURATION], when it can avert its eyes again. If the creature looks at the [MON] in the meantime, it must immediately make the save. If the [MON] sees itself reflected on a polished surface within [#] ft of it and in an area of bright light, the [MON] is, due to its curse, affected by its own gaze.

When the [MON] drops to 0 hit points outside its resting place, the [MON] transforms into a cloud of mist instead of falling unconscious, provided that it isn't in sunlight or running water. If it can't transform, it is destroyed. While it has 0 hit points in mist form, it can't revert to its [MON] form, and it must reach its resting place within [DURATION] or be destroyed. While in mist form it can't take any actions, speak, or manipulate objects. It is weightless, has a flying speed of [#] ft, can hover, and can enter a hostile creature's space and stop there. In addition, if air can pass through a space, the mist can do so without squeezing, and it can't pass through water. It has advantage on Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution saving throws, and it is immune to all nonmagical damage, except the damage it takes from sunlight. Once in its resting place, it reverts to its [MON] form. It is then paralyzed [DURATION]. After spending [DURATION] in its resting place with 0 hit points, it regains 1 hit point.

The [MON] can use its action to split into four individual swarms of tiny bone posthumes. Each swarm has an hit points total equal to the [MON]'s hit points divided by 4 (rounded down), and all are affected by any conditions, spells, and other magical effects that affected the [MON]. The [MON]s act on the same initiative count as the [MON] did and occupy any unoccupied space that previously contained the [MON]. A bone swarm can occupy another creature's space and vice versa, and the [MON] can move through a space as narrow as 1 ft wide without squeezing. A swarm can't regain hit points or gain temporary hit points. As an action, the [MON]s can reform into a single [MON] as long as all surviving swarms are within [#] ft of each other. The reformed [MON]'s hit points total is equal to the combined remaining hit points of the [MON]s, and the [MON] is affected by any conditions, spells, and other magical effects currently affecting any of the [MON]s. It occupies any unoccupied space that previously contained at least one of the [MON]s that formed it.

feature.ability_tags: Healing, Obscuring, Random Effects, Restoring, Shapechanging, Summoning
feature.desc: A creature that picks a [MON]'s fruit or is struck by Fruit Bomb triggers the fruit is chaotic magic. The [MON]'s lantern is immune to damage, and can't be the target of spells or effects as long as the [MON] lives. When the [MON] dies, the lantern floats gently to the ground and opens, if it was closed. The lantern has AC [#], [#] hit points, and is immune to piercing, poison, and psychic damage. A creature that touches the lantern must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or be cursed. A cursed creature is frightened of darkness, can't see anything outside of the lantern's light, and is unable to drop the lantern. The cursed creature will risk its own life to protect the lantern. A target can repeat this saving throw each day at dawn, lifting the curse and ending the effects on itself on a success. If this occurs, the lantern disintegrates. After three failed saving throws, remove curse or similar magic is required to end the curse. If the creature remains cursed after [DURATION], it is irreversibly changed by the curse, and it becomes the lantern's new [MON]. Voluntarily opening the lantern counts as a failed saving throw. If the lantern is destroyed, all captured spirits are put to rest and the cursed bearer, if it has not yet changed into a [MON], is freed of the curse.

feature.ability_tags: Confusing, Cursing, HP Max Reducing, Random Effects, Speed Change
feature.desc:
When the [MON] scores a critical hit against a target, it damages not only the creature, but also the threads of its fate, changing the target's past or future. The target must roll 1d6 on the chart below for each critical hit that isn't negated by a successful DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw: 
1: Seeing the Alternates: The target suffers the effects of the confusion spell [DURATION]. 
2: Untied from the Loom: The target's speed is randomized [DURATION]. Roll 3d20 at the start of each of the target's turns to determine its speed in feet [DURATION]. 
3: Shifting Memories: The target suffers a permanent -2 penalty to a random skill and gains a +2 bonus to a random skill. 
4: Not So Fast: The target loses the use of one class ability, chosen at random. 
5: Lost Potential: One of the target's ability scores, chosen at random, is reduced by 1 point. 
6: Took the Lesser Path: The target's current hit point total becomes its hit point max. 
Unless otherwise stated, these effects are permanent until the target must succeed on a [ABILITY] saving throw. The saving throw is repeated after every long rest, but the DC increases by 1 after every long rest, as the target becomes more entrenched in its new destiny. Otherwise, these new fates can be undone by nothing short of a wish spell or similar magic.

feature.desc: Whenever the [MON] takes at least [#] slashing damage at one time, roll a d20 to determine what else happens to it: (1-10) Nothing else happens. (11-14) One leg is severed from the [MON] if it has any legs left. A severed leg is unable to attack and has a speed of 5 ft. The [MON]'s speed is halved if it is missing a leg. If it loses both legs, it is knocked prone. If it has both arms, it can crawl. With only one arm, it can still crawl, but its speed is halved. With no arms or legs, its speed is 0, and it can't benefit from bonuses to speed. (1518) One arm is severed from the [MON] if it has any arms left. Each time the [MON] loses an arm, it loses a claw attack. A severed arm has a speed of 5 ft and can make one claw attack on its turn, with disadvantage on the attack roll unless the [MON] can see the arm and its target. (19-20) The [MON] is decapitated. If the [MON] dies, so does the severed head. If its head is severed, the [MON] loses its bite attack and its body is blinded unless the head can see it. The severed head has a speed of 0 ft and the [MON]'s Keen Smell trait. It can make a bite attack but only against a target in its space. If the [MON] finishes a short or long rest without reattaching a severed limb or head, the part regrows. At that point, the severed part dies. Until then, a severed part acts on the [MON]'s initiative and has its own action and movement. A severed part has AC [#], [#] hit points, and the [MON]'s Regeneration trait. The [MON] dies only if it can't regenerate.

If the [MON] goes a week without exposure to a single beast or humanoid, it loses all of its traits and reverts back to its true, blue crystalline form.

The [MON] launches its tongue at target up to [#] ft away. If the target is Small or smaller must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] Strength saving throw or be pulled up to [#] ft toward the make a DC [SAVE_DC] Constitution saving throw. If the target is Medium or larger must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or make a DC [SAVE_DC] Constitution saving throw is pulled up to [#] ft closer to the target. If the target is within [#] ft of make a DC [SAVE_DC] Constitution saving throw, it can make one melee attack against it as a bonus action.

As a bonus action, the [MON] targets any creature, object, or magical effect within [#] ft of it. The [MON] chooses a spell already cast on the target. If the spell is of 3rd level or lower, the [MON] absorbs the spell and it ends. If the spell is of 4th level or higher, the [MON] must make a spellcasting ability check. The DC equals 10 + the spell's level. On a successful check, the [MON] absorbs the spell and it ends. The [MON]'s body glows when it absorbs a spell, as if under the effect of a light spell. A [MON] can only hold one absorbed spell at a time.

As a bonus action, the [MON] designates a creature it can see within [#] ft of it and obscures the creature and its companions' travel on a particular shadow road. That shadow road will not open for the designated creature or its traveling companions except through powerful magical means such as by a key of Veles. In addition, that shadow road won't lead to its usual destination for the designated creature or its traveling companions, instead leading the group in a meandering loop. This effect lasts [DURATION], until the [MON] removes the effect, or [DURATION].

As a bonus action, the [MON] can spit a sticky, acidic web in a [#] ft cube. The webs must either be anchored between two solid masses (such as walls) or layered 5 ft deep over a flat surface. The web is difficult terrain and lightly obscures the area. A creature that starts its turn in the web or enters the web during its turn must make a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw, taking [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a success. The web persists [DURATION] before collapsing. The [MON] is immune to the effects of its web and the webs of other [MON]s.

As a bonus action, the [MON] projects a shadow on a surface within [#] ft of it. The [MON] can shape it to resemble the shadow of any beast, but the shadow can't be larger than a [#] ft cube. Each creature that starts its turn within [#] ft of the shadow and that can see the shadow must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or be incapacitated [DURATION] and use its movement on its next turn to follow the shadow. As a bonus action, the [MON] can move the shadow up to [#] ft along a solid surface. The shadow moves in a natural manner for the type of creature it represents.

If the [MON] moves through another creature, it can use a bonus action to corrupt that creature's soul. The target creature must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw. A creature paralyzed by the [MON] has disadvantage on this saving throw or suffers from terrible and violent thoughts and tendencies. Over the course of [DURATION], its alignment shifts to chaotic evil. A creature that dies during this time, or after this shift is complete, rises [DURATION] later as a [MON]. The corruption can be reversed by a remove curse spell or similar magic used before the creature's death.

As a bonus action, the creator can see through the [MON]'s eyes and hear what it hears [DURATION], gaining the benefits of the [MON]'s darkvision. During this time, the creator is deaf and blind with regard to its own senses. While using the construct's senses, the creator can cast a spell through the [MON], using those senses to target the spell. The range, area, and effect of the spell are calculated as if the spell originated from the [MON], not the master, though the master must still cast the spell on the master's turn. Spells that require concentration must be maintained by the master.

The [MON] sings a magical melody and dances. Each humanoid within [#] ft of the [MON] that can hear the revels must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or be charmed until the revels end. For every [MON] that joins in the revels, the save DC increases by 1 (maximum DC [SAVE_DC]). Each [MON] participating in the revels must take a bonus action on its subsequent turns to continue singing and must use its move action to move at least 5 ft to continue dancing. It can keep singing and dancing for [DURATION]. The song ends if all of the [MON] lose concentration or stop singing and dancing.

The [MON] can sense water within [#] ft of it that was drawn from its bonded source within the last [DURATION]. As a bonus action, the [MON] can poison up to 1 gallon of water within [#] ft of it that was drawn from its bonded source. This can even affect water that has been used to make another nonmagical substance, such as soup or tea, or water that was consumed within the last [DURATION]. The poison can affect a target through contact or ingestion. A creature subjected to this poison must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or take [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage and be poisoned [DURATION].

As a bonus action, the [MON] can disperse, scattering its parts in a [#] ft cube, centered on the space it previously occupied. A creature moving through a space containing any of the [MON]'s parts must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or stop moving this turn and take [#] [DMG_TYPE] damage. Taking this damage reduces the creature's walking speed by [#] ft [DURATION]. A creature moving through the area at half speed doesn't need to make the save. While scattered, the [MON] can't attack or move, except to reform, and it can't be targeted by attacks or spells. It can still take damage from spells that deal damage in an area.

The [MON] duplicates itself, creating four replicas. Each replica uses the statistics of an axe beak, except it also has the [MON]'s Many Eyes and Self-made Pack traits. The [MON] can communicate telepathically with a replica as long as they are within [#] ft of each other. The replicas act as allies of the [MON] and obey its telepathic commands. The replicas remain until killed or dismissed by the [MON] as a bonus action. Slain or dismissed replicas melt into a foul-smelling puddle of green goo. A replica that survives [DURATION] breaks its telepathic link with the [MON], becoming a free-thinking creature, and grows into a full [MON] after 1 month.

As a bonus action, the [MON] touches a Medium or larger tree that is not a creature and disappears inside it. While inside the tree, the [MON] has tremorsense with a radius of [#] ft, has an AC of [#], has a speed of 0, and has vulnerability to fire damage. When the [MON] is reduced to [#] hit points, the tree dies and the [MON] appears within [#] ft of the dead tree or in the nearest unoccupied space. The [MON] can exit the tree as a bonus action, appearing within [#] ft of the tree in the nearest unoccupied space, and the tree reverts to being an object. The [MON] can inhabit a tree for only [DURATION] at most before the tree dies, requiring the [MON] to seek another vessel.

The [MON] sprays pheromone-laced spores calling nearby beasts to feast. Arrive in [DURATION] and act as the [MON] allies attacking creatures within [#] ft of it. Beasts remain [DURATION]. Choose one CR 1 or lower beast or roll d100 to choose Summoned beasts. They arrive at the [MON]'s location; aggressive and prioritize active threats before feasting on creatures knocked out. Summoned beasts: 01-04: 2d4 badgers; 05-09: 1d6 black bears; 10-13: 1d3 brown bears; 14-17: 1d3 dire wolves; 18-20: 1d6 giant badgers; 21-30: 2d6 giant rats; 31-34: 1d3 giant vultures; 35-40: 2d6 giant weasels; 41-44: 1d3 lions or tigers; 45-60: 1d6 swarms of rats; 61-71: 2d4 wolves; 72-75: 1d4 worgs; 76-100: No beasts respond.

The target takes [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage (DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] half). The [MON] regains hit points equal to half the damage dealt. If the [MON] is at its hit point max it gains temporary hit points [DURATION] instead. The [MON] can add temporary hit points gained from this trait to temporary hit points gained earlier from this trait. Temporary hit points can't exceed [#]. If its temporary hit points would exceed 48 a new the [MON] appears in an unoccupied space within [#] ft of the [MON]. The new Ooze is Small doesn't have this bonus action and has [#] hit points. Creature killed by this bonus action is fully subsumed into the [MON] and can be restored to life only by means of a resurrection spell or similar magic.

The [MON] transforms into a [#] ft radius whirlwind of the treasures of which it is composed. In this form, it has immunity to all slashing and piercing damage. As a whirlwind, it can enter other creatures' spaces and stop there. Every creature in a space the whirlwind occupies must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or take [#dX] + [DMG_MOD] [DMG_TYPE] damage, and the whirlwind removes the most valuable visible item on the target, including wielded items, but not armor. If the saving throw is successful, the target takes half the bludgeoning damage, and retains all possessions. The [MON] can remain in whirlwind form [DURATION], or it can transform back to its normal form on any of its turns as a bonus action.

The [MON] can alter nearby creatures' knowledge of the forest, choosing one of the following. An effect lasts [DURATION], until the creature leaves the [MON]'s forest, or [DURATION]. (1) Remove Knowledge: Each creature within [#] ft of the [MON] must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or be hopelessly lost in the [MON]'s forest. The creature has disadvantage on Wisdom (Survival) checks and takes 50 percent more time on overland travel, even delaying clearheaded companions. (2) Share Knowledge: Each creature within [#] ft of the [MON] has advantage on Wisdom (Survival) checks. The creature can move at a fast pace through forest terrain, and difficult terrain composed of nonmagical plants doesn't cost it extra movement.

The [MON] targets one creature within [#] ft of it whose fate has been corrupted. The target creature must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or a portion of the [MON]'s consciousness inhabits its body. The target retains control of its body, but the [MON] can control its actions [DURATION] each day and can modify its memories as a bonus action (as if using the modify memory spell, DC [SAVE_DC]). The target is unaware of the [MON]'s presence, but can make a DC [SAVE_DC] Wisdom (Insight) check once every [DURATION] to notice the presence of the [MON]. This effect lasts until the [MON] ends it or the target's fate is restored by a dispel evil and good spell or similar magic. A single [MON] can seize up to four strands at the same time.

If the [MON] reduces a target to 0 hit points, the [MON] can devour that creature's soul as a bonus action. The victim must make a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw. Success means the target is dead but can be restored to life by normal means. Failure means the target's soul is consumed by the [MON] and the target can't be restored to life with clone, raise dead, or reincarnation. A resurrection, miracle, or wish spell can return the target to life, but only if the caster succeeds on a DC [SAVE_DC] spellcasting check. If the [MON] is killed within [#] ft of its victim's corpse and the victim has been dead for no longer than [DURATION], the victim's soul returns to the body and restores it to life, leaving the victim unconscious and stable with 0 hit points.

If the [MON] is dealt a critical hit with a slashing weapon, one of its extremities is severed. The extremity has AC [#], [#] hit points, a speed of 10, and the [MON]'s Regeneration trait. The [MON] controls the severed extremity and perceives through it with the appropriate senses (for instance, it sees through the eyes of its severed head). As a bonus action, the [MON] can reattach the extremity. While the [MON] is missing the extremity, its maximum hit points are reduced by 10. Roll d6 to determine the severed extremity: (1-4) Arm: If the [MON] has an arm, it loses an arm. It loses one of its claw attacks, and the severed arm can make a claw attack. (5-6) Head: If the [MON] has a head, it loses its head. It loses its bite attack, and the severed head can make a bite attack.

bonus.ability_tags: Ability Score Damage, Attaching, Ongoing Damage
bonus.desc: As a bonus action, the [MON] can attach its lamprey-like maw to a sleeping creature. The target's Charisma score is reduced by [#dX] when the [MON] first attaches to it. The target's Charisma score is then reduced by 1 for each hour the [MON] stays attached. The target dies if this reduces its Charisma to 0. Otherwise, the reduction lasts [DURATION] at least [DURATION] after the [MON] reduced its Charisma. While attached, the [MON] fills the target's dreams with nightmares. The target must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or it doesn't gain any benefit from its current rest. If the target succeeds on the saving throw by 5 or more, it immediately awakens. The [MON] can detach itself by spending 5 ft of its movement. It does so after it reduces the target's Charisma by 8 or if the target dies.

As a bonus action, the [MON] detaches its head. The head trails entrails like flexible tentacles. While detached, the head and body act independently from each other on the same initiative, and each has hit points equal to half its hit points before detaching its head. Its statistics remain the same in both forms, except the body loses its truesight and gains blindsight out to a range of [#] ft. The head and body can use the whole form's innate spellcasting trait, expending daily uses as normal. The two forms can rejoin into the [MON]'s whole form as a bonus action if they are within [#] ft of each other. If the head is destroyed while it is detached, the body also perishes. If the body is destroyed while the head is detached, the head has disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks until it acquires a new body.

The [MON] targets one humanoid it can see within [#] ft of it that has a CR up to 1/2. The humanoid must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or be charmed by the [MON]. The [MON] can telepathically communicate with any creature it has charmed. The charmed target can't take reactions and obeys the [MON]'s verbal and telepathic commands. A [MON] can have up to twelve charmed thralls at one time. A charmed thrall loses the memories of its previous life and devotes itself to the [MON] and the cult. The charm lasts [DURATION] or until the [MON] is destroyed, is more than [#] ft from the charmed target, or takes a bonus action to end the effect. The [MON] can attempt to reassert control over all of its thralls by using this action. Each thrall can repeat this saving throw when the [MON] uses this action to reassert control.

The [MON] transforms into a Huge fiend, or back into a shapeless mass. Its statistics are the same in each form, and it can't regain hit points or gain temporary hit points. If a creature is more than [#] ft away from the [MON], it must use an action to visually inspect the [MON] form and succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] Intelligence (Investigation) check to discern the Huge fiend is actually a [MON] of Small insects. A creature within [#] ft of the [MON] immediately discerns the truth. While in fiend form, it can wield weapons and hold, grasp, push, pull, or interact with objects that might otherwise require a more humanoid form to accomplish. If the [MON] takes thunder damage while in its fiend form, it immediately changes to its shapeless form. While in shapeless form, it can occupy another creature's space and vice versa and can move through any opening large enough for a Small fiend, but it can't grapple or be grappled.

One humanoid within [#] ft of it must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or be possessed by the [MON]. The possessed creature is unconscious. The [MON] enters the creatures body and takes control of it. The [MON] can be targeted only by effects that turn undead and it retains its Intelligence Wisdom and Charisma. It grants its host body immunity to being charmed and frightened. It otherwise uses the possessed creatures statistics and actions instead of its own. It doesn't gain access to the creatures memories but does gain access to proficiencies nonmagical class features and traits and nonmagical actions. It can't use limited-used abilities or class traits that require spending a resource. The possession ends after [DURATION] when the body drops to 0 hit points when the [MON] ends it as a bonus action or when the [MON] is turned or affected by dispel evil and good or a similar effect. Additionally the possessed creature repeats its saving throw whenever it takes damage. When the possession ends the [MON] reappears in a space within [#] ft of the body.

The [MON] absorbs blood that is spilled nearby into itself. This reservoir of blood grows when a creature takes extra damage from the [MON]'s Blood Lure trait. The Blood Reservoir can't exceed the [MON]'s hit point max. As a bonus action, the [MON] can reduce the Blood Reservoir by 10 to cause one of the following effects: * Empower Blood. A ally within [#] ft of the [MON] that isn't an undead or a construct has advantage on its next weapon attack roll. * Inspire Fury. A creature of the [MON]'s choice within [#] ft of the [MON] must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or immediately use its reaction to move up to its speed and make one melee weapon attack against its nearest ally. If no ally is near enough to move to and attack, the target attacks the nearest creature that isn't the [MON]. If no creature other than the [MON] is near enough to move to and attack, the target stalks off in a random direction, seeking a target for its fury. * Sustain. A nonhostile undead creature within [#] ft of the [MON] that must eat or drink, such as a ghoul or vampire, regains 10 hit points.

As a bonus action, the [MON] can start emitting a powerful, strobing light. It rapidly alternates between shedding bright light in a [#] ft radius and shedding no light, creating a dizzying effect unless the area's ambient light is bright light. Each creature within [#] ft of the [MON] and that can see the light must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or be blinded [DURATION]. A blinded creature can repeat this saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. Unless surprised, a creature with a shield or other similarly-sized object can use its reaction to raise the object and protect its eyes from the light, avoiding the saving throw. If it does so, it can't use that object for anything else. For example, a creature using a shield to protect its eyes loses the shield's bonus to its AC while using the shield in this way. If the creature looks at the [MON] or lowers or uses the object protecting its eyes, it must immediately make the save. While emitting light, the [MON] can't attack. It can stop emitting light at any time (no action required).

One humanoid that the [MON] can see within [#] ft of it must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] Charisma saving throw or the [MON] merges with it, becoming an enjoyable, repetitive tune in its host's mind. The [MON] can't be targeted by any attack, spell, or other effect. The target retains control of its body and is aware of the [MON]'s presence only as a melody, not as a living entity. The target no longer needs to eat or drink, gains the [MON]'s Magic Resistance trait, and has advantage on Charisma checks. It also has disadvantage on Wisdom saving throws and it can't maintain concentration on spells or other effects for more than a single turn. The target can make a DC [SAVE_DC] Wisdom (Insight) check once every [DURATION]; on a success, it realizes that the music it hears comes from an external entity. The Aural Symbiosis lasts [DURATION], or the [MON] is forced out by a dispel evil and good spell or similar magic. When the Aural Symbiosis ends, the [MON] bursts forth in a thunderous explosion of sound and reappears in an unoccupied space within [#] ft of the target. All creatures within [#] ft of it, including the original target, take [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage, or half damage with a successful DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw.

bonus.ability_tags: Blinding, Disadvantage, Disarming, Silencing, Speed Change, Stunning, Suffocating
bonus.desc: As a bonus action, a [MON] can turn rings, necklaces, and other jewelry momentarily against their wearer. The [MON] can affect any visible item of jewelry on up to two creatures within [#] ft of it, twisting them into cruel barbs and spikes. An item is treated as jewelry if it is made of a precious material (such as silver, gold, ivory, or adamantine), adorned with gems, or both, and is worth at least 100 gp. Each target must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw, taking [#dX] + [DMG_MOD] [DMG_TYPE] damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a success. If the jewelry is worn near the eyes, the target must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or be permanently blinded. If the jewelry is worn on the head, the target must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or have disadvantage on Intelligence checks [DURATION]. If the jewelry is worn on the neck, the target must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or be stunned and unable to breathe or speak [DURATION]. If the jewelry is worn on the arms, the target must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or deal half damage on all melee attacks [DURATION]. If the jewelry is worn on the hand, the target must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or drop any item it is holding. If the jewelry is worn on the feet, the target must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or have its speed halved [DURATION]. If the jewelry is worn elsewhere, there are no additional effects.
bonus.save_type: Wisdom, Dexterity, Dexterity, Constitution, Strength, Strength, Dexterity

reaction.desc: As a reaction when the [MON] takes damage, it uses Moan.
The [MON] halves the damage from one attack that hits it.
As a reaction when the [MON] takes damage, it uses Teleport.
As a reaction, the [MON] succeeds on a saving throw it failed.
As a reaction when the [MON] is dealt damage, they drink a potion.
As a reaction when missed by an attack, the [MON] can make one melee attack.
The [MON] can disengage after an attack reduces it to [#] hit points or less.
As a reaction, the [MON] gains advantage on one attack roll or one saving throw.
As a reaction, the [MON] adds [#] to its AC against one attack that would hit it.
As a reaction when the [MON] takes falling damage, it may reduce the damage by half.
The [MON] imposes disadvantage on an attack roll against an ally within [#] ft of it.
As a reaction when the [MON] is hit by an opportunity attack, it makes a melee attack.
As a reaction when the [MON] takes damage, it can reduce the damage it takes by [#dX].
As a reaction, the [MON] adds [#] to its AC against one melee attack that would hit it.
As a reaction when the [MON] takes fire it can immediately use Icicle Drop if available.
As a reaction, the [MON] adds [#] to its AC against one ranged attack that would hit it.
The [MON] can cast magic missile as a reaction when it is hit by a ranged weapon attack.
As a reaction when damaged by a melee weapon attack, the [MON] can make one melee attack.
As a reaction when it takes damage from an attack, the [MON] becomes invisible [DURATION].
As a reaction, the [MON] adds its Athletics bonus to its AC against one attack that would hit it.
The [MON] imposes disadvantage on an attack roll made against an ally within [#] ft of the [MON].
The [MON] uses Sweet Promises on a creature that attacked it or attempted to target it with a spell.
As a reaction when reduced to 0 hit points, the [MON] makes one final spit venom attack before dying.
As a reaction when the [MON] reduces a creature to 0 hit points, it gains [#dX] temporary hit points.
As a reaction when a creature moves within [#] ft of the [MON], the [MON] can cast the misty step spell.
As a reaction when the [MON] takes damage from a melee attack, the [MON] moves up to half its fly speed.
As a reaction, the [MON] adds [#] to its AC against one melee or ranged weapon attack that would hit it.
As a reaction when the [MON] would take fire damage from a single source, it reduces that fire damage to 0.
As a reaction when the [MON] is targeted with a melee attack, it can make one melee attack against the attacker.
As a reaction when a creature moves to within [#] ft of the [MON], the [MON] can fly up to half its flying speed.
The [MON] can move [#] ft as a reaction when it is attacked. No opportunity attacks are triggered by this movement.
As a reaction when the [MON] takes [DMG_TYPE] damage, it moves up to its speed without provoking opportunity attacks.
As a reaction when the [MON] takes damage from a creature within [#] ft of it, it uses Presage Death on the attacker.
As a reaction, the [MON] adds [#] to its AC or its mount's AC against one melee attack that would hit it or its mount.
As a reaction when an attacker the [MON] can see hits it with an attack, the [MON] halves the attacks damage against it.
As a reaction when the [MON] is hit with a melee weapon attack, the [MON] grants itself resistance to the attack's damage.
As a reaction when the [MON] is reduced to 0 hit points, it can target all creatures within [#] ft of it that can hear it.
As a reaction when a [MON] takes [DMG_TYPE] damage, it can make one melee attack against each creature within [#] ft of it.
As a reaction when a creature within [#] ft of it hits the [MON]'s owner with a melee attack, the [MON] bites the attacker.
As a reaction, the [MON] reduces the damage it takes from a single source to 0. Radiant damage can only be reduced by half.
As a reaction when a prone creature within [#] ft of the [MON] stands up from prone the [MON] can make one melee against it.
As a reaction when a creature the [MON] can see misses it with an attack, the [MON] can cast vicious mockery on the attacker.
As a reaction when a creature the [MON] can see is knocked prone, the [MON] can move up to half its speed toward the creature.
As a reaction when a creature the [MON] can see targets it with an attack, the [MON] can impose disadvantage on the attack roll.
As a reaction when an attacker that the [MON] can see hits them with an attack, the [MON] halves the attacks damage against them.
As a reaction when the [MON] is hit by a melee attack made by a creature it can see, it makes a melee attack against the attacker.
As a reaction when the [MON] takes damage, it can reduce the damage it takes by [#dX], provided that the damage is not [DMG_TYPE].
As a reaction when a creature makes an opportunity attack on the [MON], the [MON] attacks with either its bite or its tail stinger.
As a reaction when the [MON] takes damage, it gains resistance to that type of damage, including the triggering damage, [DURATION].
As a reaction when a creature attempts to grapple the [MON], the [MON] can make one melee attack against that creature as a reaction.
As a reaction when a creature the [MON] can see targets it with a melee attack, the [MON] can impose disadvantage on the attack roll.
As a reaction when an attacker the [MON] can see hits it with an attack, the [MON] can use its reaction to halve the damage it takes.
As a reaction when the [MON] is hit by a weapon attack, it gains resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage [DURATION].
As a reaction when a [MON] is dealt [#] damage or more by a single attack and survives, it can make a melee attack against the attacker.
As a reaction when a creature moves within [#] ft of the [MON], the [MON] can move up to its speed without provoking opportunity attacks.
As a reaction when damaged by a ranged weapon attack, spell, or magical effect, the [MON] targets a [#] ft long line that is [#] ft wide.
As a reaction when a creature the [MON] can see hits it with a melee weapon attack, the [MON] makes one melee attack against the attacker.
As a reaction when a creature within [#] ft of the [MON] moves away from it, the [MON] can move up to half its speed toward that creature.
As a reaction when a [MON] is hit with an attack, it can let out a blood-curdling scream. Each creature within [#] ft of the [MON] [OUTCOME].
As a reaction when a creature the [MON] can see within [#] ft of it hits the [MON] with a melee attack, the [MON] makes an attack against it.
As a reaction when a creature hits the [MON] with melee attack while within [#] ft of the [MON] the [MON] can make one melee attack against it.
As a reaction when a creature the [MON] can see within [#] ft of it regains hit points, the [MON] regains hit points equal to half that amount.
As a reaction when a creature within [#] ft of it [MON] would be hit with a melee attack, the [MON] can impose disadvantage on the attack roll.
As a reaction when the [MON] is attacked, it gains resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks [DURATION].
As a reaction when an attacker within [#] ft of the [MON] misses it with a melee attack, the [MON] can make a melee attack against the attacker.
If a creature charmed in this way moves within [#] ft of the [MON], the [MON] can use its reaction to make one attack with advantage against it.
As a reaction when the [MON] or a creature within [#] ft of it is attacked, the [MON] can interpose a wing and impose disadvantage on the attack.
As a reaction when the [MON] takes [DMG_TYPE] damage, it gains resistance to [DMG_TYPE] damage, including from the triggering attack, [DURATION].
As a reaction when a creature within [#] ft of it that the [MON] can see hits the [MON] with an attack, the [MON] uses Stone Gaze on the attacker.
As a reaction when the [MON] is hit by a melee attack by a creature within [#] ft of it, the [MON] can make one melee attack against the attacker.
As a reaction when the [MON] is within [#] ft of its master when the master takes damage, half the damage (rounded up) is transferred to the [MON].
As a reaction when the [MON]'s rider is the target of an attack the [MON] can see, the [MON] can choose to become the target of the attack instead.
The [MON] summons the wind to break the fall of up to [#] falling creatures it can see within [#] ft of it. This works like the feather fall spell.
