As a reaction when a spell that restores hit points is cast within [#] ft of the [MON], the [MON] can cause that spell to inflict damage instead of curing it. The damage equals the hit points the spell would have cured, and it is split evenly between the caster and the target(s) of the spell.

As a reaction when a creature within [#] ft of it that the [MON] can see targets it with an attack, the [MON] can stop the attacker with a glance. The attacker must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or immediately stop the attack. The attacker can't attack the [MON] again [DURATION].

As a reaction when a rakshasa the [MON] can see within [#] ft of it is the target of an attack the [MON] can move up to half its speed toward that rakshasa without provoking opportunity attacks. If it ends this movement within [#] ft of the rakshasa the [MON] becomes the target of the attack instead.

As a reaction when the [MON] is hit by a melee attack by a creature it can see within [#] ft of it, the [MON] kicks its attacker. The target must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or take [#dX] + [DMG_MOD] [DMG_TYPE] damage and be pushed up to [#] ft from the [MON] and knocked prone.

As a reaction when a [MON] that is Medium or larger is subjected to [DMG_TYPE] or [DMG_TYPE] damage, it splits into two new [MON]s if it has at least [#] hit points. Each new [MON] has hit points equal to half the original [MON]'s, rounded down. New [MON]s are one size smaller than the original [MON].

As a reaction when the [MON] takes acid, cold, force, lightning, or thunder damage, it can attune itself to that type of damage. [DURATION], the [MON] has resistance to damage of the triggering type, and when it hits with any weapon attack, the target takes an extra [#dX] damage of the triggering type.

As a reaction when a [MON] is attacked by a creature it can see within [#] ft of it, the [MON] can haunt the creature with a vision of the creature's death. The haunted creature has disadvantage on its next attack roll. Undead creatures and creatures that are unable to be killed are immune to this reaction.

As a reaction when reduced below 10 hit points (even below 0 hit points), the [MON] releases a hail of needles as a reaction. All creatures within [#] ft of it must make a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw, taking [#dX] + [DMG_MOD] [DMG_TYPE] damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a success.

As a reaction when undead under its control is reduced to 0 hit points [MON] can force it to explode. Each creature that isn't undead or [MON] within [#] ft of exploding undead: [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage (if zombie) or slashing (if skeleton) damage plus [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage (DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] half).

As a reaction when the [MON] succeeds on a saving throw against a hostile creature spell, the [MON] doesn't suffer the effects of that spell. If it uses Void Casting on its next turn, the [MON] can affect all creatures hit by its spell or who fail a saving throw against its spell instead of just one creature.

As a reaction, the [MON] issues a special command or warning when a nonhostile creature that it can see within [#] ft of it makes an attack roll or a saving throw. The creature can add a d4 to its roll, provided it can hear and understand the [MON]. A creature can benefit from only one Leadership die at a time.

As a reaction when a creature the [MON] can see starts its turn within [#] ft of the [MON], the [MON] can create the illusion that it looks like that creature's most recently departed loved one. If the creature can see the [MON], it must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or be stunned [DURATION].

As a reaction when a creature the [MON] can see within [#] ft of it is targeted with an attack, the [MON] can pull the target out of harm's way. If the creature is willing, it is pulled up to [#] ft closer to the [MON], and the [MON] becomes the new attack target. If a creature isn't willing, this reaction fails.

As a reaction when the [MON] is hit with a melee attack, it can drain blood from the attacker. The attacker must make a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw, taking [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a success. The [MON] gains temporary hit points equal to the necrotic damage taken.

As a reaction when reduced to [#] hit points or less it feigns death in hopes of deceiving its attackers. A creature that sees it in this state can determine it is a ruse via DC [SAVE_DC] Wisdom (Medicine) check. Ruse lasts [DURATION] up to [DURATION]. 1st attack it makes within [DURATION] of ending ruse has advantage.

The [MON]'s tentacles glow when a spell is cast within [#] ft of it, countering the spell. This reaction works like the counterspell spell, except the [MON] must always make a spellcasting ability check, no matter the spell level. Its ability check for this is +5. If it successfully counters the spell, the [MON] feeds.

As a reaction when a creature the [MON] can see within [#] ft of it targets it with an attack [MON] can make a Strength (Intimidation) check taking half a step forward snarling or otherwise spooking the attacker. If check is equal to or higher than attack roll attacker must reroll the attack using lower of the two results.

The [MON] catches a glimpse of an attack just before it lands, giving it time to react. As a reaction when a creature the [MON] can see hits it with a melee attack, the attacker has disadvantage on the attack roll. Alternatively, when the [MON] misses with a melee weapon attack, it can reroll the attack roll with advantage.

reaction.ability_tags: Disadvantage, Magic Disrupting, Recharging, Self Healing
reaction.desc: As a reaction when a spell is cast within [#] ft of it, the [MON] absorbs some of the spell's potency. If it is a spell that forces a saving throw, the DC to succeed drops by 2. If it is a spell with an attack roll, the attack roll has disadvantage. The [MON] regains 20 hit points and gains 1 charge point in its Arcane Pool.

As a reaction when a creature within [#] ft of the [MON] hits it with a melee attack, the [MON] can immediately use its reaction to batter the attacker with its tail. The attacker must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or take [#dX] + [DMG_MOD] [DMG_TYPE] damage, and be pushed [#] ft from the [MON] and knocked prone.

If the [MON] succeeds on a save against a spell of up to level [#] that targets only the [MON], the spell has no effect. If the [MON] succeeds on the saving throw by 5 or more, the spell is reflected back at the spellcaster using the same slot level and the spell save DC, attack bonus, and spellcasting ability of the original caster.

As a reaction when a creature charmed by the [MON] begins its turn, the [MON] telepathically commands the charmed creature [DURATION]. If the [MON] commands the creature to use an action that would harm itself or an ally, the creature must make a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw. On a success, the creatures turn immediately ends.

As a reaction when a creature the [MON] can see within [#] ft of it hits it with a spell or attack that requires a ranged attack roll, the [MON] strikes the attacker with a doom bolt. The doom bolt is a shadowy reflection of the original attack, using the same attack roll and effects as the original, except it deals [DMG_TYPE] damage.

As a reaction when the [MON]'s master is targeted by an attack or spell, the [MON] teleports to an unoccupied space within [#] ft of the master, and the attack or spell targets the [MON] instead. If the attack or spell deals damage, the [MON] takes half damage from it. To use this ability, the master and [MON] must be on the same plane.

As a reaction when a creature the [MON] can see targets it with an attack, the [MON] can switch places with any creature it can see within [#] ft of it. An unwilling creature must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw to avoid the switch. If the switch is successful, the switched creature becomes the target of the attack instead.

As a reaction when an opponent within [#] ft of the [MON] tries to cast a spell, the [MON] can emit a shriek from its twin steam whistles. The spellcaster must make a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw. If the save succeeds, the spell is cast normally. If it fails, the spell is not cast; the spell slot is not used, but the caster's action is.

As a reaction when a creature the [MON] can see within [#] ft of it casts a spell using a [#]rd-level or lower spell slot, the [MON] attempts to steal its power. The caster must make a DC [SAVE_DC] saving throw using its spellcasting ability. On a failure, the spell fails, and the [MON] gains [#dX] temporary hit points per level of the spell slot used.

As a reaction when a creature the [MON] can see within [#] ft of it casts a spell, the [MON] can absorb the spell's energy, countering it. This works like counterspell, except the [MON] must always make a spellcasting ability check no matter the spell's level. If the [MON] successfully counters the spell, it gains 5 temporary hit points per spell level.

As a reaction when a creature enters a space within [#] ft of the [MON], it can use its reaction to release a burst of fire from its clockwork hand. The target must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or take [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage and have disadvantage on the next attack roll it makes against the [MON] before the end of the [MON]'s next turn.

As a reaction when the [MON] is wrestling a foe as part of a challenge and takes damage, or when it is reduced to half its hit point max, it becomes angry. While angry, the [MON] has advantage on melee attack rolls and on saving throws against spells or effects that would charm or frighten it or make it unconscious, and it has resistance to bludgeoning damage.

As a reaction when the [MON] is hit by a ranged attack, it can create a small rift in space to increase its AC by an amount equal to its Intelligence modifier. If the attack misses as a result, the [MON] can choose a creature within [#] ft of it to become the new target for that attack. Use the original attack roll to determine if the attack hits the new target.

As a reaction when the [MON] is in the area of a spell, such as fireball, or a breath weapon, it can create a hole in the spell or breath weapon, protecting itself from the effects. If it does so, the [MON] automatically succeeds on its saving throw against the spell or breath weapon and takes no damage if it would normally take half damage on a successful save.

As a reaction when one or more [MON]s that are and share a collective mind are within [#] ft of each other, they can combine into a new [MON]. The new [MON] is one size larger than the largest original creature, and it has hit points equal to the combined total of the original creatures. The new [MON]'s hit points can't exceed the normal hit point max of a Medium [MON].

As a reaction when a [MON] that is Small or larger takes bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage, it can split into two new [MON]s if it has at least [#] hit points. Each new [MON] has hit points equal to half the original creature, rounded down. New [MON]s are one size smaller than the original. While within 1 mile of each other, the new [MON]s share one collective mind.

As a reaction when the [MON] succeeds on a saving throw, it can use its reaction to respond with a scathing magical insult if the source of the effect is a creature within [#] ft of the [MON]. That creature must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or take [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage and have disadvantage on the next save it makes against a spell cast by the [MON].

As a reaction when a creature the [MON] can see within [#] ft of it casts a spell, the [MON] counters it. This reaction works like the counterspell spell, except the [MON] can only counter spells that directly affect or create earth or stone, such as stone shape, wall of stone, or move earth, and it doesn't need to make a spellcasting ability check, regardless of the spell's level.

As a reaction when a creature hits [MON] with an attack [MON] shrieks a one-word command. Attacker must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or carry out this command on its next turn. This reaction works like the command spell except the attacker doesn't have to understand the [MON]'s language. The [MON] must see the attacker and be able to speak to use this reaction.

reaction.ability_tags: Blinding, Damage Reduction, Disadvantage, Nonreactive, Self Healing, Zero Speed
reaction.desc: As a reaction when the [MON] takes [#] damage or more from a single attack or spell, it retracts its head and limbs into its shell. It immediately regains [#] hit points. While retracted, it is blinded; its speed is 0; it can't take reactions; it has advantage on saving throws; attacks against it have disadvantage; and it has resistance to all damage. The [MON] stays retracted [DURATION].

As a reaction when the [MON] is hit by an attack, it surrounds itself in a fiery nimbus. The attacker takes [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage plus [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage, and the [MON] sheds bright light in [#] ft radius and dim light for an additional [#] ft. [DURATION], a creature within [#] ft of the [MON] that hits it with melee attack takes [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage plus [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage.

As a reaction when a creature misses the [MON] with a melee attack, the [MON] makes a weapon attack against that creature. On a hit, the target is impaled by the [MON]'s weapon and grappled (escape DC [SAVE_DC]). [DURATION], the [MON] can't make attacks with this weapon, but the target takes [#dX] + [DMG_MOD] [DMG_TYPE] damage plus [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage at the beginning of each of its turns.

As a reaction when host dies [MON] can reanimate it [DURATION] if body is still intact. During this time host protected from decay and can't become undead. The [MON] can use bonus action to cause host to move as in life but host can't take other actions. If host could speak in life [MON] can speak with host's voice. Host reanimated this way can be restored to life by any spell capable of that.

As a reaction when a creature the [MON] can see targets it with a melee attack while within [#] ft of the [MON], the [MON] can teleport to a puddle created by its Foul Transit, if that puddle's space is unoccupied, negating the damage from the attack. If it does, the attacker must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or take [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage, and become poisoned [DURATION].

As a reaction when the [MON] reduces a creature to 0 hit points, it can utter a triumphant roar. Each ally within [#] ft of the [MON] that is frightened, paralyzed, stunned, or unconscious has advantage on its next saving throw. A ally without those conditions has advantage on its next attack roll. In addition each ally within [#] ft of the [MON] that can hear it gains [#dX] temporary hit points.

As a reaction when damaged by a creature within [#] ft of the [MON] that can see it, the [MON] momentarily assumes the magical illusory form of one of the attacker's enemies or loved ones, alive or dead. The illusory figure may speak words that only the attacker can hear. The attacker must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or take [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage and be frightened [DURATION].

As a reaction when 1+ creatures step onto a space on ground within [#] ft of it directly above a hidden [MON] can burrow up to [#] ft and snap its wing-like appendages shut emerging on the ground in space directly above where it was buried and that contains one or more other creatures. Each creature must make a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or be trapped as if it failed save against Wing Trap.

As a reaction when it takes damage while below half its hit point max it creates a spectral [MON]. Spectral [MON] uses the stats of a shadow except it doesn't have Sunlight Weakness trait and can't make new shadows when it kills humanoids. It appears in an unoccupied space within [#] ft of the [MON] and acts on same initiative as that [MON]. After spectral [MON] finishes a long rest it becomes a [MON].

As a reaction when a creature tries to enter a space adjacent to a [MON], the [MON] flares its many feelers and spikes. The creature can't enter a space adjacent to the [MON] unless it succeeds on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw. If the saving throw fails, the creature can keep moving, but only into spaces that aren't within [#] ft of the [MON], and it takes [#dX] + [DMG_MOD] [DMG_TYPE] damage from the spikes.

The [MON]'s awareness of the near future allows it to see attacks before they happen. As a reaction when a creature the [MON] can see attacks it while within [#] ft of it, the [MON] can attack the creature before the creature's attack hits. The [MON] makes a single melee attack against the creature. If the creature is reduced to 0 hit points as a result of the [MON]'s attack, the creature's attack doesn't hit the [MON].

As a reaction when the [MON] takes damage or is restrained, it transforms into an incorporeal form of pure moonlight [DURATION]. While in this form, it has resistance to cold, fire, and lightning damage, and immunity to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks. While in this form, the [MON] can pass through openings at least 1 inch wide and through transparent objects. It takes [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage if it ends its turn inside an object.

As a reaction when a creature the [MON] can see targets it with an attack, the [MON] can unleash a line of strong wind [#] ft long and [#] ft wide in the direction of the attacker. The wind lasts [DURATION]. Each creature in the wind when it appears or that starts its turn in the wind must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or be pushed [#] ft away from the [MON] in a direction following the line. Any creature in the line treats all movement as difficult terrain.

As a reaction when it is attacked, the [MON] can force the attacker to make a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw if it can hear the [MON]. If the saving throw fails, the creature still attacks, but it must choose a different target creature. An ally must be chosen if no other hostile creatures are within the attack's reach or range. If no other target is in the attack's range or reach, the attack is still made (and ammunition or a spell slot is expended, if appropriate) but it automatically misses and has no effect.

If enough damage is dealt to the [MON] to kill it, it can attempt to temporarily borrow time from another creature to avoid death. One creature the [MON] can see within [#] ft of it must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or take [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage, and the [MON] regains hit points equal to the damage taken. The target is stable and doesn't die if this effect reduces its hit points to 0. after [DURATION], the [MON] takes necrotic damage, and the target regains hit points, equal to the original amount borrowed.

As a reaction when a creature the [MON] can see within [#] ft of it starts its turn or casts a spell, the [MON] issues forth a string of insults cleverly crafted to make a foe cry. If it can hear the [MON], the target must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] Wisdom saving throw or sob uncontrollably [DURATION]. A sobbing creature has disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls and must make a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw to cast a spell that requires the spellcaster to see its target. A spellcaster doesn't lose the spell slot on a failure.

As a reaction when the [MON] is first brought below half of its maximum hit points, it immediately recharges its breath weapon, if its not already available. After doing so, the air around it becomes electrically charged. A creature that starts its turn within [#] ft of the [MON] or moves within [#] ft of it for the first time on a turn must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or take [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage, and can't take reactions [DURATION]. Creatures in metal armor or wielding metal weapons have disadvantage on this saving throw.

As a reaction when a creature that can see the [MON] starts its turn within [#] ft of the [MON], the [MON] can force it to make a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw if the [MON] isn't incapacitated and can see the creature. On a failed save, the creature is incapacitated [DURATION]. Unless surprised, a creature can avert its eyes to avoid the saving throw at the start of its turn. If it does so, it can't see the [MON] [DURATION], when it can avert its eyes again. If the creature looks at the [MON] in the meantime, it must immediately make the save.

As a reaction when hit by a melee weapon attack, the [MON] can reduce the damage by [#dX] + [DMG_MOD]. If this reduces the damage to 0, the [MON] can catch the weapon if it has a free limb. To do so, it must make a Strength (Athletics) check, contested by the attacker's Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check (target chooses). The [MON] has disadvantage on the check if the weapon is wielded by two or more hands. If the [MON] wins, it disarms the creature and can throw the weapon up to [#] ft in a random direction as part of the same reaction.

As a reaction when the [MON] takes bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage, it can regurgitate some of its stomach contents. Each creature within [#] ft of the [MON] must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or take [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage and be poisoned [DURATION]. On a success, a creature takes half as much damage only. A pool of Void infused stomach contents forms in a space the [MON] can see within [#] ft of it and lasts [DURATION]. A creature that enters this pool for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there takes [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage.

reaction.ability_tags: Consumption Effect, Extra Damage, Poisoning, Toppling
reaction.desc: As a reaction when a creature the [MON] can see hits it with an attack while within [#] ft of it, the [MON] regurgitates a portion of its stomach contents on the attacker. The target must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or be poisoned [DURATION]. If the [MON] has a consumed creature when it uses this reaction, the [MON] must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or also regurgitate the swallowed creature, which is knocked prone in a space within [#] ft of the target. If it regurgitates the swallowed creature, the target and the swallowed creature take [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage.

As a reaction when a creature poisoned by the [MON] starts its turn, the [MON] can use its reaction to demand that the target repent. If the target repents, its next action is chosen by the [MON] as if it failed a save against the command spell: "Draw Nigh" (approach); "Clasp Hands in Prayer" (drop); "Seek Redemption" (flee); "Be Penitent" (grovel); or "In Stillness, Hear the Truth" (halt). If the target doesn't repent, it must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or be reduced to 0 hit points. On a success, it takes [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage. Once the [MON] has used this reaction, it must deal poison damage to a poisoned target before it can do so again.

As a reaction when a creature that can see the [MON] starts its turn within [#] ft of it [MON] can force it to make a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw if the [MON] isn't incapacitated and can see the creature. Fail: creature is mesmerized [DURATION]. Mesmerized creature over 5 ft away from [MON] must move on its turn toward the [MON] by most direct route trying to get within [#] ft of it. It doesn't avoid opportunity attacks but before moving into damaging terrain such as lava or a pit and whenever it takes damage from a source other than the [MON] target can repeat this saving throw. Mesmerized target can also re-save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

As a reaction when a creature walks over a [MON]'s hidden burrow, the [MON] can use its reaction to attack that creature with two impaling leg attacks. The creature is considered a surprised target for both attacks. If one or both attacks hit and the target is a creature, then the [MON] and the target engage in a Strength contest. If the creature wins, it can immediately move [#] ft away from the [MON]. If the contest results in a tie, the creature is grappled (escape DC [SAVE_DC]). If the [MON] wins, the creature is grappled and dragged by the [MON] [#] ft into its lair. If the creature is still grappled at the start of the [MON]'s next turn, it becomes restrained instead. The restrained creature can escape by using an action to make a successful DC [SAVE_DC] Strength (Athletics) check.

As a reaction when a [MON] feels threatened it is touched, intimidated, cornered, attacked, or even just if a stranger moves adjacent to the [MON] it immediately grows from size Small to Huge as a reaction. If the [MON] was attacked, this reaction occurs after the attack is made but before damage is done. Nearby creatures and objects are pushed to the nearest available space and must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or be knocked prone. Weapons, armor, and other objects worn or carried by the [MON] grow (and shrink again) proportionally when it changes size. Overcome by raw emotion, it sets about destroying anything and everything it can see (which isn't much) and reach (which is quite a lot). The transformation lasts until the [MON] is unaware of any nearby creatures [DURATION], until it has 5 levels of exhaustion, or it is affected by a calm emotions spell or similar magic. The transformation isn't entirely uncontrollable; people or creatures the [MON] knows and trusts can be near it without triggering the reaction.

outcome.desc: gains the Magic Resistance trait.
gains one of the following abilities [DURATION].

is coated in paint. Roll a die. Even result: target is coated in a warm color paint such as red orange or yellow. Odd result: target is coated in a cool color paint such as blue green or purple. A creature including target can use its action to remove the paint.
is knocked prone, pinned to the ground by the spike, and restrained. As an action, the restrained creature or a creature within [#] ft of it can make a [#d].

is enraged [DURATION]. While enraged, a creature has advantage on melee attacks, it is unable to distinguish friend from foe, and it must move to and attack the nearest creature other than the [MON]. If there are no creature's near enough to move to and attack, the enraged creature dashes off in a random direction. Attacks against an enraged creature have advantage.

is dominated by the [MON] (as the dominate person spell). The [MON] instantly enters the target's space and merges into the target's physical form. While inhabiting a creature, a [MON] takes no damage from physical attacks. The creature creature receives a +[#] bonus to its Dexterity and Charisma scores while it is inhabited. The speech and actions of an inhabited creature are noticeably jerky and erratic to any creature with passive Wisdom (Perception) [SAVE_DC] or higher. Each time the [MON] uses innate spellcasting, the host can attempt another DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw. A successful save expels the [MON], which appears in an unoccupied space within [#] ft of the former host. The inhabiting [MON] slowly burns out its host's nervous system. The inhabited creature must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw at the end of each day or take [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage, and have its maximum hit points reduced by the same amount. The reduction lasts until the inhabited creature completes a long rest after the [MON] is expelled.
takes [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage at the start of each of its turns.
catches on fire taking [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage at the start of each of its turns.

outcome.ability_name: Burn at the End of Your Turn
outcome.desc: ignites. The target takes [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage at the end of each of its turns.

outcome.ability_name: Burn at the Start of Your Turn
outcome.desc: ignites. The target takes [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage at the start of each of its turns.
takes [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] or [DMG_TYPE] damage (the [MON]'s choice) at the start of each of its turns.
begins bleeding. A bleeding creature loses another [#] hpoints at the start of each of its turns [DURATION].
takes [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage at the start of each of its turns until a creature uses an action to extinguish the flame on the target.
takes [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage at the end of its next turn, unless it or a creature within reach of it uses an action to clean itself off.
catches fire. Until someone uses an action to douse the fire, the creature takes [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage at the start of each of its turns.
catches on fire, taking an additional [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage at the start of each of its turns until someone uses an action to douse the fire.
is coated in burning acid. A creature coated in acid takes [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage plus [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage at the start of each of its turns.
catches on fire. Until a creature on fire uses an action to douse the fire, the creature takes [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage at the start of each of its turns.
laughs [DURATION]. While laughing, a creature is incapacitated can't speak coherently and takes [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage at the start of each of its turns.
catches on fire. Until it or another creature uses an action to douse the fire, the creature takes [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage at the start of each of its turns.
is covered in acid. At the start of each of its turns, it takes [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage until it or another creature uses an action to scrape or wash off the acid.
takes [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage at the start of each of its turns. A creature can end the ongoing damage by bandaging the wound as an action or by giving the target magical healing.

secondaryEffect.ability_name: Outcome if Not Construct or Undead
secondaryEffect.desc: If the target is a creature other than a construct or undead, it [OUTCOME].
After doing so, the [MON] can swim [#] ft without provoking opportunity attacks.
A second creature of the [MON]'s choice within [#] ft of the first target [OUTCOME].
Unsecured objects weighing 300 pounds or less are pushed [#] ft away from the [MON].
After doing so, the [MON] can make one additional attack as part of that same action.

secondaryEffect.ability_name: Outcome if Very High Attack Roll
secondaryEffect.desc: If the [MON]'s attack roll exceeds the target's AC by [#] or more, the target [OUTCOME].
If the target is a flammable object that isn't being worn or carried, it also catches fire.
After doing so, the [MON] flies up to its flying speed without provoking opportunity attacks.
If the target is a creature or flammable object that isn't being worn or carried, it [OUTCOME].
After doing so, the [MON] swims up to half its swimming speed without provoking opportunity attacks.
If a creature has immunity to [DMG_TYPE] damage, this immunity becomes [DMG_TYPE] resistance [DURATION].
If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage at the start of its next turn.
If the [MON] moved at least [#] ft straight toward a target before making an attack, the target [OUTCOME].
After doing so, the [MON] gains half cover against all attacks that originate more than [#] ft away from it.
If the target is disheartened, its hit point max is reduced by an amount equal to the [DMG_TYPE] damage taken.
If the target is a shapechanger, it instantly reverts to its true form and can't assume a different form [DURATION].
After doing so, the [MON] expels all consumed creatures, which are knocked prone in a space within [#] ft of the [MON].
After doing so, if the [MON] has movement remaining, it drags the grappled creature into deep water, where it begins suffocating.
If the target is holding or carrying one or more healing potions, there is a 25 percent chance one potion shatters, allowing the [MON] to absorb it and be healed for the corresponding amount.

After doing so, the [MON] is surrounded by a [#] ft radius sphere of smoke, which heavily obscures the area [DURATION]. A wind of moderate or greater speed (at least 10 miles per hour) disperses the smoke.

If the [MON] has half its hit points or fewer, when it does so, each target in that area must succeed on a DC [SAVE_DC] [ABILITY] saving throw or take [#dX] + [DMG_MOD] [DMG_TYPE] damage and be knocked prone.

The target takes an extra [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage and catches on fire, taking [#dX] [DMG_TYPE] damage at the start of each of its turns. The target can end this damage by using its action to make a DC [SAVE_DC] Dexterity check to extinguish the flames.

weaponMasteries.Description: If the [MON] hits a creature with a melee attack roll using this weapon, it can make a melee attack roll with the weapon against a second creature within 5 feet of the first that is also within its reach. On a hit, the second creature takes the weapon’s damage, but don't add the [MON]'s ability modifier to that damage unless that modifier is negative. The [MON] can make this extra attack only once per turn.

If the [MON]'s attack roll with this weapon misses a creature, it can deal damage to that creature equal to the ability modifier it used to make the attack roll. This damage is the same type dealt by the weapon, and the damage can be increased only by increasing the ability modifier.
When the [MON] makes the extra attack of the Light property, it can make it as part of the Attack action instead of as a Bonus Action. It can make this extra attack only once per turn.
If the [MON] hits a creature with this weapon, it can push the creature up to 10 feet straight away from itself if it is Large or smaller.
If the [MON] hits a creature with this weapon, that creature has disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of the [MON]'s next turn.

If the [MON] hits a creature with this weapon and deals damage to it, it can reduce the target's speed by 10 feet until the start of the [MON]'s next turn. If the creature is hit more than once by weapons that have this property, the speed reduction doesn’t exceed 10 feet.

If the [MON] hits a creature with this weapon, it can force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus the ability modifier used to make the attack roll and your Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, the creature has the Prone condition.
If the [MON] hits a creature with this weapon and deals damage to the creature, it has Advantage on its next attack roll against that creature before the end of its next turn.

You can use a weapon that has the ammunition property to make a ranged attack only if you have ammunition to fire from the weapon. Each time you attack with the weapon, you expend one piece of ammunition. Drawing the ammunition from a quiver, case, or other container is part of the attack. Loading a one-handed weapon requires a free hand. At the end of the battle, you can recover half your expended ammunition by taking a minute to search the battlefield. If you use a weapon that has the ammunition property to make a melee attack, you treat the weapon as an improvised weapon. A sling must be loaded to deal any damage when used in this way.
When making an attack with a finesse weapon, you use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.
Creatures that are Small or Tiny have disadvantage on attack rolls with heavy weapons. A heavy weapon's size and bulk make it too large for a Small or Tiny creature to use effectively.
A light weapon is small and easy to handle, making it ideal for use when fighting with two weapons.

Because of the time required to load this weapon, you can fire only one piece of ammunition from it when you use an action, bonus action, or reaction to fire it, regardless of the number of attacks you can normally make.

A weapon that can be used to make a ranged attack has a range shown in parentheses after the ammunition or thrown property. The range lists two numbers. The first is the weapon’s normal range in feet, and the second indicates the weapon’s maximum range. When attacking a target beyond normal range, you have disadvantage on the attack roll. You can’t attack a target beyond the weapon’s long range.
This weapon adds 5 feet to your reach when you attack with it. This property also determines your reach for opportunity attacks with a reach weapon.

If a weapon has the thrown property, you can throw the weapon to make a ranged attack. If the weapon is a melee weapon, you use the same ability modifier for that attack roll and damage roll that you would use for a melee attack with the weapon. For example, if you throw a handaxe, you use your Strength, but if you throw a dagger, you can use either your Strength or your Dexterity, since the dagger has the finesse property.
This weapon requires two hands to use. This property is relevant only when you attack with the weapon, not when you simply hold it.
This weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property—the damage when the weapon is used with two hands to make a melee attack.

You can use a weapon that has the Ammunition property to make a ranged attack only if you have ammunition to fire from it. The type of ammunition required is specified with the weapon's range. Each attack expends one piece of ammunition. Drawing the ammunition is part of the attack (you need a free hand to load a one-handed weapon). After a fight, you can spend 1 minute to recover half the ammunition (round down) you used in the fight; the rest is lost.
When making an attack with a Finesse weapon, use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.
You have Disadvantage on attack rolls with a Heavy weapon if it's a Melee weapon and your Strength score isn't at least 13 or if it's a Ranged weapon and your Dexterity score isn't at least 13.

When you take the Attack action on your turn and attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a different Light weapon, and you don’t add your ability modifier to the extra attack’s damage unless that modifier is negative. For example, you can attack with a Shortsword in one hand and a Dagger in the other using the Attack action and a Bonus Action, but you don't add your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the damage roll of the Bonus Action unless that modifier is negative.
You can fire only one piece of ammunition from a Loading weapon when you use an action, a Bonus Action, or a Reaction to fire it, regardless of the number of attacks you can normally make.

A Range weapon has a range in parentheses after the Ammunition or Thrown property. The range lists two numbers. The first is the weapon’s normal range in feet, and the second is the weapon’s long range. When attacking a target beyond normal range, you have Disadvantage on the attack roll. You can't attack a target beyond the long range.
A Reach weapon adds 5 feet to your reach when you attack with it, as well as when determining your reach for Opportunity Attacks with it.

If a weapon has the Thrown property, you can throw the weapon to make a ranged attack, and you can draw that weapon as part of the attack. If the weapon is a Melee weapon, use the same ability modifier for the attack and damage rolls that you use for a melee attack with that weapon.
A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.
A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.
